items.title: Task: Operator console: /ui/runbooks/runs role-scoped runs list + start-run modal

labels.name: frontend
labels.description: Operator web UI — G10.x HTMX/Jinja console surface

items.body:
Parent goal: #336
Parent initiative: #1837

## Context

The console ships full runbook **authoring** (catalog browse + template editor + publish/deprecate, G10.6 #1381 → `ui/routes/runbooks/`) but no way to **run** a published runbook from the UI — starting a run and seeing the runs you own is `meho runbook start` / `meho runbook list-runs` (CLI) only. This Task adds the entry surface for the run lifecycle: a role-scoped runs list plus a start-run modal.

The backend run lifecycle is complete and stable: the run service + schemas land under Goal G12 #1195 (opacity-floor design #1198), and the REST routes under G12.3-T5 #1311. The list + start REST routes already exist in `backend/src/meho_backplane/api/v1/runbook_runs.py` (`@router.get("")` at `:517`, `@router.post(...)` start at `:313`); this Task is a **pure UI/BFF build** that calls the in-process `RunbookRunService` directly (BFF pattern — `require_ui_session` + service call, never the Bearer `/api/v1` surface), exactly as the read surface `ui/routes/runbooks/routes.py` calls `RunbookTemplateService()` in-process.

This is T1 of #1837. The run **driver** (`/ui/runbooks/runs/{id}` — render the current step, Advance/Abort/Reassign) is T2 and depends on this list shipping first.

## Current state

- `RunbookRunService.start_run(tenant_id, operator_sub, request: StartRunRequest) -> CurrentStepResponse` — `run_service.py:276`. Auto-assigns the caller as `assigned_to`; raises `DeprecatedTemplateError` / `TemplateNotFoundError` / `MissingParamsError`.
- `RunbookRunService.list_runs(tenant_id, caller_sub, *, caller_is_admin, filter_: ListRunsFilter, limit=100) -> list[RunSummary]` — `run_service.py:719`. The visibility split is **service-enforced**: `caller_is_admin=False` forces `assignee=caller_sub` (an OPERATOR only ever sees their own runs even if they pass `?assignee=` for someone else); `caller_is_admin=True` honours the filter as-is (TENANT_ADMIN sees all tenant runs). See the REST handler at `api/v1/runbook_runs.py:518-602` for the exact `caller_is_admin = operator.tenant_role == TenantRole.TENANT_ADMIN` derivation to mirror.
- `RunSummary` (`runbooks/runs_schemas.py:429-466`): `run_id`, `template_slug`, `template_version`, `assigned_to`, `target`, `state` (`Literal["in_progress","completed","abandoned"]`), `started_at`, optional `completed_at`/`abandoned_at`, `current_step_id`, `position: StepPosition | None`, `work_ref`. **No step body content** — the list is opaque-by-construction.
- `StartRunRequest` (`runs_schemas.py:238-263`): `template_slug: str`, `target: str`, `params: dict[str,object]` (default `{}`), `work_ref: str | None`.
- The runbooks router is built by `build_runbooks_router()` in `ui/routes/runbooks/routes.py:384` and mounted under `/ui` via `ui/routes/__init__.py:147+`. The agent-run router mounts under `/ui/agents/runs` (#1824) — **no path collision** with `/ui/runbooks/runs`.
- CSRF: double-submit per `ui/csrf.py` — every state-changing POST under `/ui/` must carry `X-CSRF-Token` (HMAC-bound to the session). The render mints with `mint_csrf_token(str(session.session_id))` and sets the JS-readable cookie via the shared `set_csrf_cookie` (`ui/routes/runbooks/editor.py:97`); the modal form echoes the token via `hx-headers` and the SAME response must refresh the cookie (the desync-on-fragment-render footgun documented in `ui/templates/memory/_create_modal.html` and `routes.py:303-334`).
- RBAC helpers to reuse (do not hand-roll): `resolve_role_probe` (soft-hide, never 5xx the read page) and `resolve_operator_or_403` (hard 403) in `ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:152,184`. For the operator-floor write here, lift the operator's `sub` from `require_ui_session` (`session.operator_sub`) — the same identity `start_run` records as `assigned_to`.

## Scope

Add a **"Runs" tab** on the existing `/ui/runbooks` surface (recommended in #1837 to keep the sidebar stable) backed by these routes, all registered in `build_runbooks_router()` **before** the `/ui/runbooks/{slug}` catch-all so the literal `runs` segment is not bound as a slug parameter (first-match-wins):

1. `GET /ui/runbooks/runs` — runs list page. Resolve `caller_is_admin` via the same role lift the read surface uses — the in-repo precedent is `_is_admin(session_ctx)` (`routes.py:207`, a thin wrapper over `_resolve_role` at `:160`), which fails soft to `False` (operator privileges) on a lift failure rather than 5xx-ing the read page. (Alternatively reuse `resolve_role_probe` from `connectors/operator.py:152` for the `is_tenant_admin` boolean.) Call `list_runs(...)` with `caller_is_admin`, building `ListRunsFilter` (`runs_schemas.py:402`). Render a DaisyUI table of `RunSummary` rows: template_slug@version, target, state badge (in_progress/completed/abandoned), assigned_to, `position` ("step n of total" when present), work_ref, started_at, and a row link to `/ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` (the T2 driver). For a TENANT_ADMIN render an `assignee` filter control; for an OPERATOR omit it (they only see their own — the service ignores it anyway). `HX-Request: true` returns only the list fragment (filter swap); direct navigation returns the full page.
2. `GET /ui/runbooks/runs/start` — HTMX-loaded start-run modal fragment (mirrors `ui/templates/memory/_create_modal.html`). Fields: `template_slug` (operator types or selects from published templates), `target`, optional `params` (JSON object textarea), optional `work_ref`. The form `hx-post`s to the start route with `hx-disabled-elt="find button[type=submit]"`. Register this literal sub-route **before** `/ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` (T2) — coordinate ordering with T2 so `start` is not swallowed by the `{run_id}` param route.
3. `POST /ui/runbooks/runs` — start handler. Operator floor. Build `StartRunRequest`, call `start_run(session.tenant_id, session.operator_sub, request)`. On success return 204 + `HX-Redirect: /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` (drop the operator straight into the T2 driver). Map `DeprecatedTemplateError` / `TemplateNotFoundError` / `MissingParamsError` to inline modal `alert-error` (not a 500) — surface the missing-params message so the operator knows which `${run.params.X}` to supply.

## Acceptance criteria

- `pytest backend/tests/.../test_ui_runbook_runs_list.py` (new): a seeded OPERATOR with one own run and another operator's run sees ONLY their own row in `GET /ui/runbooks/runs` (assert the foreign `run_id` string is absent from the HTML); a seeded TENANT_ADMIN sees both. Verifies the `caller_is_admin` branch is wired, not just the buttons hidden.
- `pytest` test: `POST /ui/runbooks/runs` with a valid published `template_slug` returns 204 with `HX-Redirect: /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` and a `RunbookRun` row lands with `assigned_to == operator.sub`; a body referencing an unsupplied `${run.params.X}` renders the modal `alert-error` (HTTP 200 fragment, not 500) carrying the missing-params message.
- `pytest` test: `POST /ui/runbooks/runs` with a missing/invalid `X-CSRF-Token` is rejected 403 by `CSRFMiddleware` (assert `x-csrf-rejection-reason` header present); the start-modal fragment render refreshes the `meho_csrf` cookie so the immediately-following submit's header matches the cookie (no `value_mismatch`).
- `grep -n` proof in `ui/routes/runbooks/routes.py` (or a new `ui/routes/runbooks/runs.py` registered from it): `/ui/runbooks/runs`, `/ui/runbooks/runs/start`, and the start POST are all registered **before** the `@router.get("/ui/runbooks/{slug}")` line, and `/ui/runbooks/runs/start` before `/ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}`.
- After adding the routes, run `cd cli && make snapshot-openapi && make generate` and commit the regenerated `cli/api/openapi.json` + `cli/internal/api/client.gen.go`; CI lane "CLI API snapshot freshness" must pass (the committed snapshot already carries 72 `/ui/*` paths — `/ui/*` routes DO register into the FastAPI app and land in the spec; the "UI-only, no snapshot change" note on #1837 is incorrect).

## Out of scope

- The run **driver** (render current step, Advance/Abort/Reassign) — T2 (#1837), depends on this list.
- Any backend change to `runbook_runs.py` / `run_service.py` — the surface is complete and stable; this is UI/BFF only.
- A bespoke SSE/live-update of the list — #1837 explicitly rules out SSE for runbook runs (strict request/response, single-assignee); run state-changes already surface on the activity feed.
- Server-side `params` schema validation beyond what `start_run` already enforces (the textarea posts a JSON object; reject non-object client-side, let `MissingParamsError` cover the rest).

## References

- Backend run service + schemas: `backend/src/meho_backplane/runbooks/run_service.py:276,719`, `backend/src/meho_backplane/runbooks/runs_schemas.py:238-263,429-466`.
- REST role-split precedent: `backend/src/meho_backplane/api/v1/runbook_runs.py:518-602`.
- Closest UI precedent (read surface + soft role lift + CSRF cookie posture): `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/routes/runbooks/routes.py` (`_resolve_role:160`, `_render_index:271`, `_set_csrf_cookie:240`, ordering note `:393`).
- Modal precedent: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/templates/memory/_create_modal.html`; write-handler precedent: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/routes/runbooks/lifecycle.py`.
- RBAC lift helpers: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:152,184`; session gate: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/auth/middleware.py:426`. CSRF: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/csrf.py`.
- Framework anchors (versions pinned in repo): HTMX 2.0.9 (`hx-get`/`hx-post`/`hx-disabled-elt`/`HX-Request`/`HX-Redirect`) https://htmx.org/reference/ ; DaisyUI 5.5.20 table/badge/modal; Jinja2 3.1.6; FastAPI `>=0.136.3,<0.137` `APIRouter`; Pydantic 2.13.4. Convention authority is the in-repo `ui/routes/runbooks/` surface (the best-practices packs cited by /new-ticket do not exist in this checkout).

items.title: Windows: Server crashes with access violation after repeated column type modifications via PREPARE/EXECUTE in stored procedure
items.body:
## Description

When running the `yonyou_test.yonyou` mysqltest suite on a Windows installation of SeekDB, the server's background thread crashes with an access violation exception. The client connection is lost with error 2013. The crash log is provided below.

## Environment
- Platform: Windows
- Version: seekdb (OceanBase seekdb) source revision 1-ebf82ac7a6f1b940f0a5f36ea8bedefeeb626658

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On the machine, navigate to the directory: `/obdata/data/AndroidTest/ob_opensource_test/tools/deploy`
2. Execute the following commands to set up the test environment and run the specific test set:
```bash
export OCEANBASE_HOME=/obdata/data/AndroidTest/ob_opensource_test/
cd ${OCEANBASE_HOME}/tools/deploy
source activate_obd.sh
export OBD_SEEKDB_STATUS_FALLBACK_TCP=1

obd test mysqltest test_env --mysqltest-bin=${OCEANBASE_HOME}/deps/3rd/u01/obclient/bin/mysqltest --obclient-bin=${OCEANBASE_HOME}/deps/3rd/u01/obclient/bin/obclient --init-only --init-sql-dir=${OCEANBASE_HOME}/tools/deploy --init-sql-files='init.sql,init_user.sql|root@sys|test'
obd test mysqltest test_env --mysqltest-bin=${OCEANBASE_HOME}/deps/3rd/u01/obclient/bin/mysqltest --obclient-bin=${OCEANBASE_HOME}/deps/3rd/u01/obclient/bin/obclient --disable-reboot --test-set=yonyou_test.yonyou
```
3. The crash occurs during the execution of a stored procedure `p_aa_updatecolumn` that uses `PREPARE`/`EXECUTE` to repeatedly modify the data type of the same column (`bAutoflt`) on table `pb_filter_solution_common`. The specific SQL sequence that triggers the crash (error 2013) is:
```sql
USE test;

SET NAMES utf8mb4;
SET sql_mode = 'NO_AUTO_VALUE_ON_ZERO';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS `pb_filter_solution_common`;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `pb_filter_solution_common` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `solutionId` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `itemName` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `itemId` bigint(20) DEFAULT NULL,
  `itemTitle` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `refType` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `isCommon` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `rangeInput` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `multSelect` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `compareLogic` enum('is_not_null','is_null','between','like','rightlike','leftlike','egt','elt','gt','lt','neq','nin','in','eq') DEFAULT NULL,
  `defaultVal1` varchar(5000) DEFAULT NULL,
  `defaultVal2` varchar(5000) DEFAULT NULL,
  `orderId` float(255,0) DEFAULT NULL,
  `saveHistory` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `checkRefer` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `pb_filter_solution_commoncol` varchar(45) DEFAULT NULL,
  `tenant_id` bigint(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `defineId` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '自定义项对应字段',
  `itemType` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,
  `refercode` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `bhidden` bit(1) DEFAULT b'0',
  `isshoprelated` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0' COMMENT '是否门店相关',
  `cEnumType` varchar(40) DEFAULT NULL,
  `bEnum` tinyint(4) DEFAULT NULL,
  `bAutoflt` tinyint(4) DEFAULT NULL,
  `cDataRule` varchar(200) DEFAULT NULL,
  `itemTitle_resid` varchar(200) DEFAULT NULL,
  `iType` smallint(1) DEFAULT '0' COMMENT '字段类型(为null或0搜索；1排序；2搜索和排序)',
  `defaultOrder` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '默认顺序 asc/desc',
  `cExtProps` text,
  `cDesignProps` text,
  `ytenant_id` varchar(36) DEFAULT '~',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `pb_filter_solution_common_tenant_id_idx` (`tenant_id`),
  KEY `i_solutionId_tenant_id` (`solutionId`,`tenant_id`),
  KEY `userdefineid_tenant_id_idx` (`tenant_id`,`defineId`),
  KEY `idx_filter_solution_common_id` (`solutionId`,`tenant_id`),
  KEY `idx_multlang_itemtitle` (`tenant_id`,`itemTitle`),
  KEY `idx_ytenant_id` (`ytenant_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB AUTO_INCREMENT=0 ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC;

DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS `p_aa_updatecolumn`;
DELIMITER //
CREATE PROCEDURE `p_aa_updatecolumn`(
  IN tablename varchar(50),
  IN columnname varchar(50),
  IN executeStr varchar(1000),
  IN executeType varchar(50)
)
BEGIN
  DECLARE CurrentDatabase VARCHAR(100);
  SELECT DATABASE INTO CurrentDatabase;
  SET @tablename = tablename;
  SET @columnname = columnname;
  SET @executeType = executeType;
  SET @executeStr = executeStr;
  SET @count = (
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.COLUMNS
    WHERE table_schema = CurrentDatabase
      AND TABLE_NAME = @tablename
      AND COLUMN_NAME = @columnname
  );
  IF @executeType = 'add' AND @count = 0 THEN
    PREPARE stmt1 FROM @executeStr;
    EXECUTE stmt1;
  ELSEIF @executeType = 'alter' AND @count > 0 THEN
    PREPARE stmt1 FROM @executeStr;
    EXECUTE stmt1;
  END IF;
END //
DELIMITER ;

-- The call sequence consistent with the mysqltest failure (the last line triggers error 2013)
CALL p_aa_updatecolumn('pb_filter_solution_common', 'cDesignProps', 'alter table `pb_filter_solution_common` modify column `cDesignProps` text   ;', 'alter');
CALL p_aa_updatecolumn('pb_filter_solution_common', 'cExtProps', 'alter table `pb_filter_solution_common` modify column `cExtProps` text   ;', 'alter');
CALL p_aa_updatecolumn('pb_filter_solution_common', 'cExtProps', 'alter table `pb_filter_solution_common` modify column `bAutoflt` smallint ;', 'alter');
CALL p_aa_updatecolumn('pb_filter_solution_common', 'cExtProps', 'alter table `pb_filter_solution_common` modify column `bAutoflt` int ;', 'alter');
CALL p_aa_updatecolumn('pb_filter_solution_common', 'cExtProps', 'alter table `pb_filter_solution_common` modify column `bAutoflt` bigint ;', 'alter');
CALL p_aa_updatecolumn('pb_filter_solution_common', 'cExtProps', 'alter table `pb_filter_solution_common` modify column `bAutoflt` varchar(20);', 'alter');
```

## Actual Result

The server crashes with an access violation in a background thread, and the process terminates. The client receives a connection lost error (2013).

**Server Log Snippet:**
```
admin@DESKTOP-5S3HHLA C:\Users\admin>"C:\Program Files\seekdb\bin\seekdb.exe" --nodaemon --base-dir C:\seekdb_data_lvw --port 6881
Starting seekdb (OceanBase seekdb) source revision 1-ebf82ac7a6f1b940f0a5f36ea8bedefeeb626658.
Change working directory to base dir. path='C:\seekdb_data_lvw\'
The log file is in the directory: 'C:\seekdb_data_lvw//log/'
[WIN32-TRACE] Vectored exception #1: code=0x80000003 addr=0x000002AF02C0274B tid=9056 (bg-thread)
  Rip=0x000002AF02C0274B RVA=0xFFFF82B7AC94274B Rsp=0x000000D6F70F3AA0 Rbp=0x00000000FFFFF05E
  StackWalk64 backtrace:
    #00 0x000002AF02C0274B (+0x0)
    #01 0x000000D6F70F3CE8 (+0x0)
    #02 0x00007FF756F395D8 (seekdb.exe+0xC795D8) [RVA=0xC795D8]
    #03 0x00007FF757EE2683 (seekdb.exe+0x1C22683) [RVA=0x1C22683]
  Stack scan (RVAs): [sp+248]=0x1C2170E [sp+312]=0xD6E11E8 [sp+440]=0x1C1B73C
[WIN32-TRACE] Background thread crash #1, terminating process to avoid corruption.
```

**Client Error (2013):**
![Client Error Screenshot](https://antsys-ark-oss.cn-shanghai-alipay-office.oss-alipay.aliyuncs.com/alipay/workitem/2026041700115482837/richtext_202604170010003068203_image.png?Expires=4898457438&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tDShzNxA19xobwoWeHq&Signature=LnGt52jWDyk1mgX8CaBHLjNpjWY%253D&response-content-disposition=attachment%253Bfilename%253Dimage.png)

**Test Failure Output:**
![Test Failure Screenshot](https://antsys-ark-oss.cn-shanghai-alipay-office.oss-alipay.aliyuncs.com/alipay/workitem/2026041700115482837/richtext_202604170010003068140_image.png?Expires=4898458040&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tDShzNxA19xobwoWeHq&Signature=ro4NUdY%252F1NULo9YqueXt7WbSep4%253D&response-content-disposition=attachment%253Bfilename%253Dimage.png)

items.title: Task: Keycloak console — client-scope + protocol-mapper authoring (tenant_admin, approval handoff)

labels.name: frontend
labels.description: Operator web UI — G10.x HTMX/Jinja console surface

items.body:
Parent goal: #336
Parent initiative: #1943

Depends-on: #1959

## Context

T1 (#1943) ships the `/ui/keycloak` read scaffold (realm config, client list/detail, client-scope list). This task adds the **client-scope and protocol-mapper authoring** writes: create a client-scope (`keycloak.client_scope.create`) and create a protocol-mapper (`keycloak.protocol_mapper.create`) — the op that wires the `tenant_id` / `tenant_role` claims the backplane row-scopes on (`connectors/keycloak/ops_write.py:394`). Today these are CLI-only via `meho keycloak client-scope create` / `meho keycloak protocol-mapper create`.

Both verbs are thin Cobra layers over `POST /api/v1/operations/call` against the pinned `connector_id="keycloak-admin-26.x"` (`cli/internal/cmd/keycloak/keycloak.go:81`). There is **no `/api/v1/keycloak` REST surface**; the console dispatches the op IDs **in-process** through `operations.meta_tools.call_operation` (`operations/meta_tools.py:1000`).

## Current state

- The ops are complete, registered, and CLI-exercised today, both `requires_approval=True` and `safety_level="caution"` (`connectors/keycloak/ops_write.py:19-20`):
  - `keycloak.client_scope.create` (`cli/internal/cmd/keycloak/client_scope.go:30` docstring / func — params `{"representation": <ClientScopeRepresentation>}`; its `protocolMappers` may ride in the body; a 409 already-exists is an idempotent success; backend `ops_write.py:362`).
  - `keycloak.protocol_mapper.create` (`cli/internal/cmd/keycloak/protocol_mapper.go:35` func, docstring `:28` — params `{"representation": <ProtocolMapperRepresentation>}` plus the target client keyed on `id` (client internal UUID) OR `client_id` (human clientId, name→UUID resolved); the CLI builds the param map at `protocol_mapper.go:65-73`; backend requires id-or-client_id at `ops_write.py:394-414`; a 409 already-exists is idempotent).
- Protocol mappers have **no dedicated read verb**; they are read via `keycloak.client.get` (they ride in the `ClientRepresentation`) — `protocol_mapper.go:20` notes the connector exposes only `create`. The "scope ↔ client" relation view reuses T1's client detail + client-scope list reads.
- In-process write precedent with confirm + CSRF + approval handoff: the MERGED `/ui/operations` Run modal (`ui/routes/operations/routes.py:480-499,825-884`).

## Desired state

In the `ui/routes/keycloak/` package (T1):

- A **create-client-scope** form + `POST /ui/keycloak/client-scopes/create` (dispatch `keycloak.client_scope.create`) — collects a `ClientScopeRepresentation` (name, protocol, attributes; optional embedded protocolMappers) → `{"representation": {...}}`.
- A **create-protocol-mapper** form + `POST /ui/keycloak/clients/{client_uuid}/protocol-mappers/create` (dispatch `keycloak.protocol_mapper.create`) — collects a `ProtocolMapperRepresentation` and keys the target client on `id` (the route's `{client_uuid}`) → `{"representation": {...}, "id": <client_uuid>}`.
- A **scope ↔ client relation view**: surface, on a client's detail (from T1's `keycloak.client.get`), which client-scopes it references, with a deep-link back to the client-scope list. Read-only assembly over T1's reads — no new read op.

Literal segments register **before** any `{param}` route (first-match-wins — the discipline `ui/routes/operations/routes.py:397` documents): `/ui/keycloak/client-scopes/create` and the literal `protocol-mappers/create` tail under `/ui/keycloak/clients/{client_uuid}`. Every write is CSRF-gated: any `POST` under `/ui/` is enforced by the `ui/csrf.py` double-submit middleware (see `ui/routes/operations/routes.py:447`). Carry the OWASP signed double-submit token on the confirm button's own `hx-headers` (HTMX does NOT inherit it to children); re-mint + re-set the `meho_csrf` cookie on a modal that rotates it — the `mint_csrf_token` / `set_csrf_cookie` pattern at `ui/routes/operations/routes.py:807,821`. Each write shows an **unmissable confirm** before POST. Because both ops are `requires_approval=True`, the dispatcher's policy gate (`operations/_validate.py::policy_gate`, imported `operations/dispatcher.py:265`, invoked `dispatcher.py:1518`) → `_handle_needs_approval` (`dispatcher.py:1352`) returns `status="awaiting_approval"` with `extras["approval_request_id"]` (contract at `dispatcher.py:101-103`); render that id + **deep-link `/ui/approvals`**.

## RBAC

**Verified gate**: the underlying dispatch is **operator-tier with a policy gate** — `call_operation` (`meta_tools.py:1000`) enforces no role itself, and the Bearer twin `POST /api/v1/operations/call` gates only on `_require_operator` = `TenantRole.OPERATOR` (`api/v1/operations.py:96,252`); `requires_approval=True` (not RBAC) routes both to `awaiting_approval`. This task **adds a BFF-layer `tenant_admin` gate** on top for both writes (create-scope / create-mapper), justified by blast radius and matching the initiative's posture and the existing UI write routes (`connectors/registry_actions.py`, `agents/routes.py`, `conventions/write.py` all gate writes with `resolve_operator_or_403`). The scope ↔ client relation read stays operator-tier.

Mirror the soft-hide / hard-403 split: `resolve_role_probe` (`ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:152`, soft-fail) drives the `is_tenant_admin` template conditional so a plain operator never sees the create buttons; the write POST handlers gate server-side with `resolve_operator_or_403` (`ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:184`; `TENANT_ADMIN` assertion + 403 raise at `operator.py:199-204`) so a forged POST from a non-admin returns 403. (NOTE: `resolve_operator_or_403`'s 403 `detail` is the connectors-specific `"re-probe requires tenant_admin"` string; render a keycloak-appropriate alert message or add a thin keycloak-local admin dependency.) Tenant scope is `operator.tenant_id` only — no tenant override param (`ui/routes/kb/routes.py` cross-tenant→404 posture).

## Acceptance criteria (all command/grep/test-verifiable)

- `pytest backend/tests/ -k "keycloak_ui and client_scope_create and awaiting_approval"` (new test): a confirmed `POST /ui/keycloak/client-scopes/create` whose dispatch returns `status="awaiting_approval"` renders the approval banner with `extras["approval_request_id"]` AND a link whose href targets `/ui/approvals`.
- New test (protocol-mapper target keying): `POST /ui/keycloak/clients/{uuid}/protocol-mappers/create` dispatches `keycloak.protocol_mapper.create` with `params` carrying `{"representation": {...}, "id": <uuid>}` (the client keyed off the route path, not a free-form field) — assert against the captured `call_operation` arguments.
- New test (confirm + CSRF): each create modal renders an unmissable confirm surfacing `caution`/requires-approval; a `POST` without the CSRF token → `403`, with it → `200`/`awaiting_approval`.
- New test (RBAC): a plain **operator** session sees the scope ↔ client relation view but NOT the create-scope / create-mapper buttons (soft-hide via `resolve_role_probe`); a forged `POST` to either write route as a non-admin returns `403` (server-side `resolve_operator_or_403`); a **tenant_admin** sees the buttons and the POST dispatches.
- `cd cli && make snapshot-openapi && make generate` is run and the regenerated `cli/api/openapi.json` + `cli/internal/api/client.gen.go` are committed (the new `/ui/keycloak/client-scopes*` + `/ui/keycloak/clients/{uuid}/protocol-mappers*` routes land in the snapshot; "CLI API snapshot freshness" CI enforces it).
- `cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy src/` clean.

## Out of scope

- Realm/client/client-scope **read** scaffold → **T1** (#1943).
- User management (list/create/reset-password/role-assign) → **T2** (#1943).
- A dedicated protocol-mapper **read** verb — none exists; mappers are read via `keycloak.client.get` (T1).
- Implementing/re-implementing the approval **decide** flow — lives on `/ui/approvals` (#1778); this task only **deep-links**.
- Any new backend route or meta-tool — BFF + template assembly only.

## References

- Initiative #1943. Depends on T1 (#1943) for the surface scaffold + client/scope reads.
- Op registration + safety/approval ground truth: `connectors/keycloak/ops_write.py:19-20` (client_scope.create / protocol_mapper.create = `caution`, `requires_approval=True`), `:362` (client_scope.create handler), `:394-414` (protocol_mapper.create — wires tenant claims; requires id-or-client_id).
- CLI op-ID + param ground truth: `cli/internal/cmd/keycloak/keycloak.go:69-81` (pinned `connector_id`), `client_scope.go:16-17,30` (`keycloak.client_scope.create` — `{"representation": ...}`), `protocol_mapper.go:20,28,35,65-73` (`keycloak.protocol_mapper.create` — `{"representation": ..., "id"|"client_id": ...}`; mappers read via `keycloak.client.get`).
- Backend dispatch + approval handoff: `operations/meta_tools.py:1000` (`call_operation`) → `:905`; `operations/_validate.py::policy_gate` (imported `operations/dispatcher.py:265`, invoked `dispatcher.py:1518`), `dispatcher.py:1352` (`_handle_needs_approval`), `dispatcher.py:101-103` (`extras["approval_request_id"]` contract).
- Precedent surfaces: `ui/routes/operations/routes.py:397,447,480-499,807,821,825-884` (route-order discipline + in-process confirm-gated POST + `ui/csrf.py` double-submit + CSRF cookie re-mint via `mint_csrf_token`/`set_csrf_cookie` + `awaiting_approval` deep-link), `ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:152` (`resolve_role_probe` soft-hide), `:184,199-204` (`resolve_operator_or_403` hard-403), `ui/routes/connectors/registry_actions.py` / `ui/routes/agents/routes.py` / `ui/routes/conventions/write.py` (existing write routes layering `resolve_operator_or_403`), `ui/csrf.py`, `ui/routes/approvals/routes.py` (CSRF on the confirm button's own `hx-headers`), `ui/routes/kb/routes.py` (no-tenant-override posture), `api/v1/operations.py:96,252` (OPERATOR-tier Bearer twin).
- Framework anchors (pinned from the checkout): HTMX 2.0.9 (`ui/static/src/vendor/VENDOR.md:25`) — `hx-post`/`hx-headers` (not inherited to children)/`hx-disabled-elt`, https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-disabled-elt/ ; Alpine.js 3.15.12 (`ui/static/src/vendor/VENDOR.md:27`) `x-data` for the confirm-modal state, https://alpinejs.dev/directives/data ; FastAPI `>=0.136.3,<0.137` (`backend/pyproject.toml:14`) `Form`/`APIRouter`; Pydantic v2 `>=2.13.4` (`backend/pyproject.toml:16`); Jinja2 `>=3.1.6` (`backend/pyproject.toml:35`).

items.title: Task: Operator console: runbook run driver (/ui/runbooks/runs/{id}) — current-step render + Advance/Abort/Reassign

labels.name: frontend
labels.description: Operator web UI — G10.x HTMX/Jinja console surface

items.body:
Parent goal: #336
Parent initiative: #1837
Depends-on: #1884

## Context

T1 of #1837 lands the runs list + start-run modal. This Task builds the **run driver** at `/ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` — the page a junior operator uses to drive a started runbook step-by-step to completion or a reasoned abort, entirely in the console, with a senior able to reassign. It is the half that closes the loop on runbooks (guided, verify-gated execution).

The backend run lifecycle land under Goal G12 #1195 (opacity-floor design #1198), with the REST routes at G12.3-T5 #1311. The **write** half is a pure UI/BFF build calling the in-process `RunbookRunService` directly (BFF: `require_ui_session`/`require_ui_admin` + service call, never the Bearer `/api/v1` surface), mirroring `ui/routes/runbooks/lifecycle.py`.

**This Task is NOT 100% pure-UI — it needs one small backend read method.** See "Current state" below: there is **no** typed service getter that returns a single run's current `StepBody`, and **no** `GET /api/v1/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` REST route (verified: the only run REST routes are `POST /{run_id}/next|abort|reassign`, `POST ""` start, `GET ""` list — `runbook_runs.py:313,366,431,480,517`). The driver's `GET /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` page has nothing to render from on a fresh navigation. This Task therefore MUST add a thin, opacity-safe service read method (returns ONLY the single current `StepBody` post-substitution, never the full step list) and call it from the BFF. Scope this explicitly — do not pretend the read path exists.

The single biggest correctness risk (per #1837's grounding pass) is the **opacity leak**: this page must render ONLY the run's current step, never the full template body — re-introducing the template steps would re-open the exact skip-ahead leak #1198 was built to close. The new read method is the load-bearing guard here: it must mirror the single-step projection that `next_step`/`start_run` return (`CurrentStepResponse` carrying exactly one `current_step`), NOT load `pinned.steps`.

## Current state

- `RunbookRunService.next_step(tenant_id, operator_sub, run_id, request: NextStepRequest) -> NextStepResponse` — `run_service.py:367`. **Fail-closed assignee gate is in the SERVICE, not role-based**: any caller other than `run.assigned_to` — **including a TENANT_ADMIN** — gets `NotRunAssigneeError` (`run_service.py:376-383`, REST maps 403 at `api/v1/runbook_runs.py:418-428`). The verify outcome branches (`run_service.py:396-406`): `next_step` → `CurrentStepResponse` (next step body); `completed` → `RunCompletedResponse`; `failed` → step marked `failed` + **`PreviousStepFailedError` raised** — after a `no`/`escalate` confirm answer the only forward path is abort. A reassign racing the dispatch makes the loser's write raise `NotRunAssigneeError` (documented at `run_service.py:413-418`).
- `RunbookRunService.abort_run(tenant_id, operator_sub, run_id, request: AbortRunRequest, *, caller_is_admin=False) -> AbortRunResponse` — `run_service.py:607`. Permits caller ∈ `{run.assigned_to, any TENANT_ADMIN}`; the route passes `caller_is_admin = operator.tenant_role == TENANT_ADMIN` (`api/v1/runbook_runs.py:467`). `AbortRunRequest.reason` is `Field(min_length=1)` (`runs_schemas.py:353-364`) — an empty reason **422s server-side** (it is persisted to the abort audit row, `run_service.py:629-635`).
- `RunbookRunService.reassign_run(tenant_id, operator_sub, run_id, request: ReassignRunRequest) -> ReassignRunResponse` — `run_service.py:679`. **TENANT_ADMIN only** — the service does NO role check; the route gate is the sole authority (`api/v1/runbook_runs.py:480-514`, `_require_admin`). `ReassignRunRequest.new_assignee` is `Field(min_length=1)` (`runs_schemas.py:377-389`).
- Shapes the page renders: `CurrentStepResponse` (`runs_schemas.py:266-291`) carries `run_id`, `template_slug`, `template_version`, `position: StepPosition` ("n of total"), and exactly one `current_step: StepBody`. `StepBody` (`runs_schemas.py:161-202`): `id`, `title`, `body` (Markdown — render with the shared `ui/routes/kb/render.render_markdown`, as `routes.py:36,221-237` does), `type` (`operation_call`/`manual`), nullable `op_id`/`params`, and `verify: StepBodyVerify`. `StepBodyVerify` (`runs_schemas.py:130-159`): `type` (`confirm`/`operation_call`), `prompt`, `op_id`, `params`, `expect` — all substitutions already resolved by the engine.
- `NextStepRequest` (`runs_schemas.py:328-350`): `last_verified: bool` (informational only — the substrate is the oracle), `verify_response: VerifyResponse | None`. For a `confirm` step the operator answers `ConfirmVerifyResponse{type:"confirm", answer: "yes"|"no"|"escalate"}` (`runs_schemas.py:83-95`); only `yes` advances, `no`/`escalate` → `failed`. For an `operation_call` verify the engine populates the response from the dispatched call — the client sends no captured result.
- **CONFIRMED GAP — a new read method is required.** The five public `RunbookRunService` methods are `start_run` (`:276`), `next_step` (`:367`), `abort_run` (`:607`), `reassign_run` (`:679`), `list_runs` (`:719`) — plus the predicate `can_show_template_post_completion` (`:811`, returns `bool`, not a step). **None returns a single run's current `StepBody`.** `list_runs` gives `RunSummary.current_step_id` + `position` but **no body** (opaque-by-construction). So a fresh `GET /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` has no service call that yields the renderable step. The POST handlers (`next`/`start`) DO return `CurrentStepResponse` and the driver re-renders that on each Advance — but the initial page load and any browser refresh need a getter. **Add a new method**, e.g. `RunbookRunService.get_current_step(tenant_id, operator_sub, run_id) -> CurrentStepResponse | RunCompletedResponse` (or an abandoned variant), that loads the run + its step states + the single current step body (post-substitution) and returns the SAME `CurrentStepResponse` projection — reusing the existing `_current_step_id_or_none` (`:942`) / `_position_from_step_id` helpers. It MUST NOT return the full step list. **Do not load the pinned template body to re-derive the current step in the template/handler — that is the opacity leak.** Because this adds no new REST route (the BFF calls the service in-process) it does not change `/api/v1`, but it DOES add a `/ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` route → snapshot regen still required (see acceptance criteria).
- RBAC/BFF wiring to reuse: operator-floor session via `require_ui_session` (`middleware.py:426`); hard TENANT_ADMIN gate for reassign via `require_ui_admin` (`middleware.py:516`); soft role hint for the page (show/hide Reassign) via `resolve_role_probe` (`connectors/operator.py:152`). CSRF double-submit per `ui/csrf.py` with the shared `set_csrf_cookie` (`editor.py:97`) re-minted on every fragment render (the cookie/header desync footgun, `routes.py:303-334`).

## Scope

Register these routes in `build_runbooks_router()` (or a `ui/routes/runbooks/driver.py` registered from it), **before** the `/ui/runbooks/{slug}` catch-all, and the literal `/ui/runbooks/runs/start` (T1) **before** `/ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` (first-match-wins):

0. **New service read method** `RunbookRunService.get_current_step(...)` returning the single-step `CurrentStepResponse` projection (or the terminal-state response for completed/abandoned runs) — see "Current state". This is the only backend change in the Task and is the opacity-safe source for the GET page.
1. `GET /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` — driver page. Call `get_current_step(session.tenant_id, session.operator_sub, run_id)`; on `RunNotFoundError` → 404 page. Render run coordinates + `position` ("step n of total") + the **single current `StepBody`** (title, Markdown-rendered body via `render_markdown` from `kb/render`, op_id/params for `operation_call`, the verify gate). Render the action controls conditionally:
   - **Advance** — shown ONLY when the session operator is the run's assignee (`session.operator_sub == run.assigned_to`). For a `confirm` verify, render the yes/no/escalate answer control; for an `operation_call` verify, render a plain Advance (engine dispatches + captures).
   - **Abort** — confirm dialog + a **required** non-empty reason textarea.
   - **Reassign** — shown ONLY for a TENANT_ADMIN (`resolve_role_probe.is_tenant_admin`); a `new_assignee` field.
2. `POST /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}/next` — operator floor. Build `NextStepRequest`, call `next_step(session.tenant_id, session.operator_sub, run_id, request)`. Re-render the step fragment from the returned `CurrentStepResponse`; on `RunCompletedResponse` render the completed state. Map `NotRunAssigneeError`→inline "you are not the assignee" / "this run was reassigned away from you" (NOT a 500); `PreviousStepFailedError`→an inline dead-end banner explaining the step failed and the only forward move is **Abort** (hide Advance); `RunAlreadyTerminalError`/`VerifyResponse*`→inline alerts.
3. `POST /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}/abort` — operator floor; pass `caller_is_admin = (probe.is_tenant_admin)`. Reject an empty reason **client-side** (HTMX `required` + a guard) AND handle the server 422 cleanly (so the audit guarantee holds even on a tampered form). On success render the abandoned state.
4. `POST /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}/reassign` — **`require_ui_admin` hard gate** (operator → 403 at the dependency, before the body). Call `reassign_run`; render the new-ownership state. After a reassign, the previous assignee's open page must show "reassigned away from you" on their next Advance (the service returns `NotRunAssigneeError` for them).

All controls echo `X-CSRF-Token` via `hx-headers`; every render re-mints the token and refreshes the `meho_csrf` cookie.

## Acceptance criteria

- `pytest backend/tests/.../test_ui_runbook_driver_opacity.py` (new): (a) the new `RunbookRunService.get_current_step(...)` returns a `CurrentStepResponse` whose `current_step.id == position` step and does NOT expose any other step (assert the returned object has no full-step-list attribute and the other steps' titles are absent from its serialization); (b) `GET /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` for an in-progress run renders ONLY the current step — assert the page HTML contains the current step's `title`/`body` and does NOT contain the title/body text of any other step in the template. Guards the opacity leak end-to-end.
- `pytest` test: `POST /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}/next` by a **non-assignee TENANT_ADMIN** renders an inline "not the assignee / reassigned away" message at HTTP 200 (assert no 500); a `confirm` step answered `no` renders the failed-step dead-end banner with Advance hidden and Abort shown (driven by `PreviousStepFailedError`).
- `pytest` test: `POST /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}/abort` with an empty `reason` is handled (client-guard + server 422 surfaced as an inline alert, not 500); with a valid reason the `RunbookRun` row flips to `abandoned` and an abort audit row lands carrying the reason.
- `pytest` test: `POST /ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}/reassign` by an OPERATOR is 403 at `require_ui_admin` (before the service is touched); by a TENANT_ADMIN it flips `assigned_to` and the prior assignee's subsequent `next` POST renders the "reassigned away from you" message.
- `grep -n` proof: `/ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}` and its `next`/`abort`/`reassign` sub-routes are registered **before** `@router.get("/ui/runbooks/{slug}")`, and `/ui/runbooks/runs/start` (T1) is registered **before** `/ui/runbooks/runs/{run_id}`; the reassign route declares `Depends(require_ui_admin)`.
- After adding the routes, run `cd cli && make snapshot-openapi && make generate` and commit the regenerated `cli/api/openapi.json` + `cli/internal/api/client.gen.go`; CI lane "CLI API snapshot freshness" must pass (these new `/ui/*` routes register into the FastAPI app and land in the spec — the "UI-only, no snapshot change" note on #1837 is incorrect).

## Out of scope

- The runs list + start modal — T1 (#1837); this Task depends on it.
- Any backend change beyond the one required read-only `get_current_step` getter on `run_service.py` (which returns ONLY the single current `StepBody`). No new `/api/v1` REST route (the BFF calls the service in-process); never widen any surface to expose the full step list. No change to `next_step`/`abort_run`/`reassign_run` semantics.
- SSE / live push of run state — #1837 rules it out (strict request/response, single-assignee); state-changes already surface on the activity feed.
- Operator self-reassign or any role-based bypass of the assignee gate — the documented escalation path is a TENANT_ADMIN reassign, by design (#1198).

## References

- Backend run service: `backend/src/meho_backplane/runbooks/run_service.py:276,367,607,679,719` (`start_run`/`next_step`/`abort_run`/`reassign_run`/`list_runs`) + `:811` (`can_show_template_post_completion`, a `bool` predicate — NOT a step getter). Helpers for the new `get_current_step`: `_current_step_id_or_none` (`:942`) + `_current_step_id_or_raise` (`:921`).
- Run schemas: `backend/src/meho_backplane/runbooks/runs_schemas.py:83-95,130-202,266-291,328-389`.
- REST gate/role precedent (mirror the `caller_is_admin` derivation + the admin-only reassign gate): `backend/src/meho_backplane/api/v1/runbook_runs.py` — `next` `:366`, `abort` `:431` (`caller_is_admin = operator.tenant_role == TenantRole.TENANT_ADMIN` at `:467`), `reassign` `:480` (`operator: Operator = _require_admin` at `:484`), `list` `:517`. NOTE: there is **no** `GET /{run_id}` REST route — the driver page's read is BFF-only via the new service getter.
- Closest UI write-surface precedent (HTMX fragment swap + `hx-swap-oob` + typed-error→inline alert + CSRF re-mint): `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/routes/runbooks/lifecycle.py`. Markdown renderer to reuse for the step body: `render_markdown` from `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/routes/kb/render.py` (imported at `routes.py:113`). NOTE: `_render_steps` (`routes.py:221`) renders the FULL `template.steps` list — that is the template-detail surface and the exact OPACITY-LEAK pattern the driver must NOT copy; the driver renders the ONE `current_step.body` only.
- RBAC/BFF: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:152` (`resolve_role_probe`); `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/auth/middleware.py:426,516` (`require_ui_session`/`require_ui_admin`). CSRF: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/csrf.py`.
- Framework anchors (versions pinned in repo): HTMX 2.0.9 (`hx-post`/`hx-swap`/`hx-swap-oob`/`hx-disabled-elt`/`hx-headers`) https://htmx.org/reference/ ; `hx-swap-oob` https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-swap-oob/ ; DaisyUI 5.5.20 alert/badge/modal; Jinja2 3.1.6; FastAPI `>=0.136.3,<0.137`; Pydantic 2.13.4; markdown-it-py 4.2.0. Convention authority is the in-repo `ui/routes/runbooks/` surface (the /new-ticket best-practices packs do not exist in this checkout).

items.title: Task: Operator console: /ui/connectors/registry list (distinct from targets) — status/product filters + confirm-gated per-row enable/disable/enable-reads/delete

labels.name: frontend
labels.description: Operator web UI — G10.x HTMX/Jinja console surface

items.body:
Parent goal: #336
Parent initiative: #1839

## Context

The connector **curation** loop (ingest a spec, review the LLM-grouped operations, govern per-op safety/approval, enable for dispatch) is CLI/MCP-only today. This Task builds the first console surface of that loop: a **connector registry list** at `/ui/connectors/registry`, distinct from the existing `/ui/connectors` **targets** list.

The two are easy to conflate, so the naming and entry point must read clearly as **Registry** vs **Targets** (initiative grounding note: "Naming collision"). The backend is fully shipped — this is pure UI/BFF, calling the in-process service the REST routes already call (the in-process-BFF pattern, never the Bearer REST route).

### Backend surface to reuse (all opened + line-verified at HEAD `7acae0d1`)

- `operations/ingest/list_connectors.py:410` — `async def list_ingested_connectors(*, operator: Operator, status: ConnectorStatusFilter | None = None, sessionmaker=None) -> list[ConnectorListItem]`. Visibility is **operator-level read**: built-ins (`tenant_id IS NULL`) plus the caller's own tenant rows; cross-tenant rows never appear (the visibility filter is `(OperationGroup.tenant_id.is_(None)) | (== operator_tenant_id)`, `list_connectors.py:319`). Call it in-process from the BFF.
- `operations/ingest/api_schemas.py:462` — `class ConnectorListItem`: `connector_id: str`, `product: str`, `version: str`, `impl_id: str`, `tenant_id: UUID | None`, `group_count`, `staged_group_count`, `enabled_group_count`, `disabled_group_count`, `operation_count`, `enabled_operation_count`, `state: ConnectorState = "ingested"`, `next_step: NextStep | None = None`. `ConnectorState = Literal["ingested","registered"]` is defined at `api_schemas.py:427`.
- `operations/ingest/api_schemas.py:89` — `ConnectorStatusFilter = Literal["staged","enabled","disabled","all"]`. The shipped REST `list_endpoint` (`connectors_ingest.py:1061`) already takes `status: ConnectorStatusFilter | None = Query(default=None)` and returns `{"connectors": [...]}` (or a v2 envelope with `?envelope=v2`).
- **`connector_id` is the operator-facing `<impl_id>-<version>` string** (e.g. `vmware-rest-9.0`), built by `build_connector_id` (`_llm_grouping_internals.py:515-523` → `return f"{impl_id}-{version}"`) and split by `parse_connector_id` (`parser.py:27`). It is **slash-free**, so the BFF routes use a **plain `{connector_id}` string path param — NOT the `:path` converter** (matching the shipped REST routes, which all use plain `{connector_id}`).
- The four write verbs this list's per-row actions invoke (each a shipped REST handler in `api/v1/connectors_ingest.py`, all gated by `_require_admin` = `TenantRole.TENANT_ADMIN`, `connectors_ingest.py:253`):
  - `POST /{connector_id}/enable` (`enable_endpoint`, `connectors_ingest.py:1263`, 204, idempotent, 409 `InvalidStateTransitionError`).
  - `POST /{connector_id}/enable-reads` (`enable_reads_endpoint`, `connectors_ingest.py:1297`, 200 `EnableReadsResponse{connector_id, ops_enabled}`, idempotent; 409 `connector_scope_ambiguous` via `build_connector_scope_ambiguous_detail`, `connectors_ingest.py:~1346`).
  - `POST /{connector_id}/disable` (`disable_endpoint`, `connectors_ingest.py:1361`, 204, idempotent, 409).
  - `DELETE /{connector_id}` (`delete_endpoint`, `connectors_ingest.py:1394`, 204; the deleted-rows count surfaces as `enabled_operations_deleted` in the `meho.connector.delete` audit payload, doc at `connectors_ingest.py:1424`, field `delete_connector.py:129`).

### Precedent UI surface (the freshest convention authority)

- `ui/routes/connectors/list_view.py` — the targets list: `_render` (`list_view.py:337`) serves the full page (`connectors/list.html`) and the HTMX `connectors/_table_rows.html` fragment, branching on `_is_htmx_request` (`list_view.py:198`). CSRF cookie mint at `list_view.py:365` (`mint_csrf_token`). `is_tenant_admin` flows into the template context at `list_view.py:389` (soft-hide of write affordances). A `_distinct_products` helper already exists at `list_view.py:269` — model the registry `?product=` dropdown on it. **Model this Task's list handler on `_render` + `build_list_router` (`list_view.py:406`).**
- `ui/routes/connectors/__init__.py:79` — `build_router()` with the load-bearing first-match-wins registration-order commentary (`__init__.py:88-105`); the router include order is `list → forms → import → detail → probe` (`__init__.py:108-112`).
- `ui/routes/connectors/operator.py` — `resolve_role_probe` (soft-hide, read paths, `operator.py:152`) returning `OperatorRoleProbe{is_tenant_admin, is_operator}` (`operator.py:68-87`) and `resolve_operator_or_403` (hard 403 to `TENANT_ADMIN`, write paths, `operator.py:184`). Reuse both; do not hand-roll the lift.
- `ui/csrf.py` — double-submit: `mint_csrf_token(session_id)` (`csrf.py:199`), `verify_csrf_token` (`csrf.py:227`), cookie `CSRF_COOKIE_NAME="meho_csrf"` (`csrf.py:122`), header `CSRF_HEADER_NAME="X-CSRF-Token"` (`csrf.py:129`). `CSRFMiddleware` enforces every non-safe (`_SAFE_METHODS={"GET","HEAD","OPTIONS"}`, `csrf.py:139`) method under the `_UI_PREFIX="/ui/"` (`csrf.py:144`).
- `ui/templates/base.html:36` — `nav_surfaces` list; the `connectors` entry → `/ui/connectors` is at `base.html:41`. Add the Registry entry/sub-nav here.
- `ui/routes/connectors/forms_router.py` — the in-process-BFF-calls-REST-handler pattern: `_edit_submit_handler` (`forms_router.py:187`) and `_delete_submit_handler` (`forms_router.py:160`) call the shipped `submit_edit`/REST handler so UI and REST share one validation + audit code path. **Model the per-row verb handlers on these.**
- `ui/templates/base.html:101-112` — the shared `modal-dialogs.js` `<dialog class="modal">` container for HTMX-injected confirm modals.

## Scope

Add a server-rendered connector-registry list surface to the console:

1. **Route + handler** — `GET /ui/connectors/registry`. One handler serving the full page (extends `base.html`) on a browser nav and a table-rows fragment on `HX-Request` (mirror `list_view._is_htmx_request`). Read RBAC = **OPERATOR**: lift via `resolve_role_probe` for the soft-hide of the write affordances, and call `list_ingested_connectors(operator=<lifted Operator>, status=<filter>)` in-process. Lift the full `Operator` for the service call the same way `operator.py` does (do not invent a new lift). Filters: `?status=staged|enabled|disabled|all` (Pydantic `ConnectorStatusFilter` enum → 422 on out-of-range) and a `?product=` exact-match dropdown computed in the handler from the distinct `product` values of the returned items (do not add a DB query the service does not need). Each row renders `connector_id`, `product`/`version`/`impl_id`, a tenant-vs-built-in chip (`tenant_id` None ⇒ "built-in"), the `state` pill (`ingested` vs `registered`), and the group/op counts (`staged_group_count`/`enabled_group_count`/`disabled_group_count`, `enabled_operation_count`/`operation_count`).
2. **Per-row actions (confirm-gated)** — `enable`, `disable`, `enable-reads`, `delete`. Each is an HTMX verb handler under a new BFF route (`POST /ui/connectors/registry/{connector_id}/enable|disable|enable-reads` and `DELETE /ui/connectors/registry/{connector_id}` for delete) that calls the matching shipped REST handler in-process (`forms_router.py:160,187` pattern) so UI and REST share validation + audit. **Use a plain `{connector_id}` string path param — `connector_id` is the slash-free `<impl_id>-<version>` string, so the `:path` converter is NOT needed** (the shipped REST verbs all use plain `{connector_id}`). Write RBAC = **TENANT_ADMIN** via `resolve_operator_or_403`. Soft-hide the action buttons from non-admins via `resolve_role_probe`/`OperatorRoleProbe.is_tenant_admin` (the `list_view.py:389` pattern). On success re-render the affected row (or table) via `hx-swap`/`hx-swap-oob`.
3. **Loosening-action confirms (governance footgun)** — `enable`, `enable-reads`, and `disable→enable` loosen the safety boundary, so each needs an explicit confirm modal showing projected blast radius (counts from the row: how many groups/ops flip). `delete` is **type-to-confirm** (operator types the `connector_id`) and the confirm copy must surface that enabled operations will be removed (the `enabled_operations_deleted` advisory, audit at `delete_connector.py:383`). Render the confirm modals as HTMX-loaded `<dialog class="modal">` fragments via the shared `modal-dialogs.js` container (`base.html:101-112`).
4. **Error panels** — render `409 connector_scope_ambiguous` (the `candidates[]` envelope from `build_connector_scope_ambiguous_detail`), `409 InvalidStateTransitionError`, and `503 LlmClientUnavailable` as actionable inline panels, not raw 500s.
5. **base.html nav** — surface the Registry as a clearly-labelled sibling of Targets (a second `nav_surfaces` entry, or a Targets/Registry tab pair under Connectors). Must read unambiguously as "Registry" vs "Targets".

## Acceptance criteria

- `GET /ui/connectors/registry` returns 200 for an authenticated operator and renders one row per item from `list_ingested_connectors`; a new pytest `tests/unit/ui/routes/connectors/test_registry_list.py::test_registry_list_renders_rows` asserts a seeded ingested connector's `connector_id` + `state` pill appear in the HTML and a cross-tenant row does **not**.
- A pytest asserts the literal `/ui/connectors/registry` route is registered **before** `/ui/connectors/{name}` in the built app router (first-match-wins): resolve `build_router()`'s route list and assert the registry path's index precedes the `{name}` detail route — guards the initiative's "Route ordering" footgun.
- A pytest asserts the four per-row verbs reject a non-tenant_admin operator with 403 (`resolve_operator_or_403`), that the action buttons are absent from the rendered HTML for a non-admin (soft-hide via `resolve_role_probe`), and present for a tenant_admin.
- A pytest asserts an `enable-reads` against a connector that maps to both a tenant and a built-in row renders the `409 connector_scope_ambiguous` `candidates[]` panel inline (not a 500), and an `InvalidStateTransitionError` 409 renders an inline panel.
- A pytest asserts every write verb requires the CSRF double-submit token (a POST without `X-CSRF-Token` is rejected by `CSRFMiddleware`), mirroring the targets-write tests against `verify_csrf_token`.
- **OpenAPI snapshot**: this Task adds new `/ui/connectors/registry*` routes to the FastAPI app, so run `cd cli && make snapshot-openapi && make generate` and commit the regenerated `cli/api/openapi.json` + `cli/internal/api/client.gen.go`; the "CLI API snapshot freshness" CI lane must be green. (The initiative body's "No OpenAPI snapshot change (UI-only)" is incorrect — `/ui/*` routes register into the app and land in the committed snapshot, proven across all of #1824's PRs.)

## Out of scope

- The ingest modal (catalog/explicit-quadruple + dry-run + async job-poll) — that is T2 (#1839).
- The review drawer with per-op `safety_level`/`requires_approval`/`is_enabled`/`custom_description` edits — that is T3 (#1839).
- Any backend route/service change. The list service, the four verbs, and the error envelopes are all shipped; if a backend behaviour seems missing, re-diagnose before filing — do not patch the backend here.
- A cross-tenant selector or built-in/global writes (those go through the MCP siblings).

## References

- Backend: `api/v1/connectors_ingest.py:1061` (list), `:1263`/`:1297`/`:1361`/`:1394` (enable/enable-reads/disable/delete), `:253` (`_require_admin`/`_require_operator`); `operations/ingest/list_connectors.py:410,319`; `operations/ingest/api_schemas.py:89,427,462`; `operations/ingest/parser.py:27` + `_llm_grouping_internals.py:515` (slash-free `connector_id`); `operations/ingest/delete_connector.py:129,383` (`enabled_operations_deleted`).
- Precedent UI: `ui/routes/connectors/list_view.py:198,269,337,365,389,406`, `ui/routes/connectors/__init__.py:79,88-112`, `ui/routes/connectors/forms_router.py:160,187`, `ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:68,152,184`, `ui/csrf.py:122,129,199,227`, `ui/templates/base.html:36,41,101-112`.
- HTMX (vendored `ui/static/src/vendor/htmx.min.js`): `HX-Request` request header (https://htmx.org/reference/#request_headers); `hx-swap-oob` (https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-swap-oob/); `hx-disabled-elt` for the double-submit guard on confirm buttons (precedent: `ui/templates/connectors/_edit_modal.html`).
- Pydantic v2 (`pydantic[email]>=2.13.4`), FastAPI (`>=0.136.3,<0.137`), Jinja2 (`>=3.1.6`) per `backend/pyproject.toml`.

items.title: Task: Vault console — confirm-gated KV writes (put CAS / delete / secret.move) with approval handoff

labels.name: frontend
labels.description: Operator web UI — G10.x HTMX/Jinja console surface

items.body:
Parent goal: #336
Parent initiative: #1942

Depends-on: #1956

## Context

T1 ships the read-only `/ui/vault` KV browser scaffold (target/mount picker → list → read → versions). This task adds the **mutating** verbs to that surface: confirm-gated `vault.kv.put` (CAS-aware), `vault.kv.delete` (soft-delete versions), and `secret.move` (references-not-values, approval-gated). These are the highest-blast-radius actions the Vault console gains — every one is `requires_approval=True`, so the gate must be unmissable and the result render must surface the approval handoff rather than a silent success.

This is **UI/BFF assembly over the existing dispatcher surface** — no new connector code. All three ops are complete + tested.

## Current state

- `vault.kv.put`: CLI `meho vault kv put` pre-bakes `vault-1.x`, dispatches `vault.kv.put` with CAS via `--cas` (`cli/internal/cmd/vault/kv.go:179-195`; `casSet = cmd.Flags().Changed("cas")` distinguishes "explicit --cas 0 / must-not-exist" from "flag absent"). Backend: `safety_level="caution"`, `requires_approval=True` (`connectors/vault/ops.py:1147-1148`); replaces the latest version wholesale (no merge).
- `vault.kv.delete`: `meho vault kv delete --versions 3,4,5` dispatches `vault.kv.delete` with `versions[]` (`cli/internal/cmd/vault/kv.go:243-254`). Backend: `safety_level="dangerous"`, `requires_approval=True` (`ops.py:1209-1210`); **reversible** soft-delete (Vault marks versions deleted, retains data until destroyed).
- `secret.move` is a **separate connector**: CLI `meho secret move` pre-bakes `connector_id="secret-broker-1.x"` (`cli/internal/cmd/secret/secret.go:57`) and dispatches op_id `secret.move` (`cli/internal/cmd/secret/move.go:18`). Backend: `safety_level="dangerous"`, `requires_approval=True` (`connectors/secret/ops.py:259-260`). Params are **references, never values**: `from`/`to` are `<kind>:<ref>` strings (`SECRET_MOVE_PARAMETER_SCHEMA`, `secret/ops.py:87`; "the schema rejects … smuggling a value field"). The response is value-free — `{status, value_sha256, length}` only, canonical key order pinned at `cli/internal/cmd/secret/move.go:140`; the value "never enters the op params, the response, a log event, or the audit row" (`secret/ops.py:250-253`).
- No `/ui/vault` write route exists (T1 ships read-only).

## Scope

Extend the T1 `ui/routes/vault/` router with the write actions. Each is a CSRF-gated `POST` under `/ui/` (the `ui/csrf.py` double-submit gate) + `require_ui_session`, dispatching `call_operation` **in-process** (`operations/meta_tools.py:1000`) — same path as `ui/routes/operations/routes.py`'s `POST /ui/operations/call` (`routes.py:457-505`, `_render_call_result` at `:825`).

- `GET /ui/vault/put/confirm` (+ `delete/confirm`, `move/confirm`) — render an **unmissable destructive-confirm modal**, modeled on the operations Run modal (`operations_run` at `routes.py:459`, `_render_run_modal` at `routes.py:776` — computes `requires_confirmation = safety_level != "safe" or requires_approval` at `routes.py:811` and renders a prominent banner). Mint + re-set the `meho_csrf` cookie on the modal render so the confirm button's OWN `hx-headers` echo lines up after the HTMX swap rotated it (`mint_csrf_token` imported at `routes.py:211`, `set_csrf_cookie` at `routes.py:212`; minted at `routes.py:807` + applied at `routes.py:821`; the #1693/#1754 cookie-desync class).
- `POST /ui/vault/put` — dispatch `vault.kv.put` (`connector_id="vault-1.x"`, target + `{mount, path, data, cas?}`). Carry `cas` only when the operator explicitly set it (mirror the CLI `Changed("cas")` rule).
- `POST /ui/vault/delete` — dispatch `vault.kv.delete` with `versions[]`.
- `POST /ui/vault/move` — dispatch `secret.move` with `connector_id="secret-broker-1.x"` and the schema's `from`/`to` reference fields (`SECRET_MOVE_PARAMETER_SCHEMA`, `secret/ops.py:87`; `additionalProperties: false` rejects a smuggled value field) **references only**. There is deliberately no value input field — keep the no-`--value` invariant the CLI keeps. Render only the value-free `{status, value_sha256, length}` confirmation (the CLI's `moveResultKeyOrder` at `cli/internal/cmd/secret/move.go:140`), never an inline value.

Each result render (mirror `_render_call_result` at `routes.py:825` → `operations/_result.html`): because every write is `requires_approval=True`, the common return is `status="awaiting_approval"` with `extras["approval_request_id"]` (built by `result_awaiting_approval`, `operations/_errors.py:251`) — surface a banner + deep-link `/ui/approvals/{approval_request_id}` (the real detail route `GET /ui/approvals/{request_id}`, `ui/routes/approvals/routes.py:386`; #1778) so the operator never thinks the op silently no-op'd. `status="error"`/`"denied"` → render `error` + `extras.error_code`. The malformed-params / missing-target `ValueError` maps to an inline 400 form error (`_render_call_form_error`, `routes.py:886`).

The literal `put` / `delete` / `move` segments register **before** any `{param}` route on the same router (first-match-wins). These are POST routes, so they cannot collide with a GET slug route regardless, but keep the declaration discipline.

## RBAC

**OPERATOR tier — no tenant_admin step.** On the sibling operations console the run/call routes are `require_ui_session`-only (no `TenantRole` dependency on the route); state-changing ops are in the OPERATOR capability set (`routes.py:471`, "Run is in the OPERATOR capability set -- no tenant_admin step"; `_render_run_modal` docstring `routes.py:797`: "the run is still OPERATOR-tier (no tenant_admin step), and the policy gate -- not RBAC -- is what escalates a requires_approval op to awaiting_approval"). The vault write ops carry NO role gate — `vault.kv.put`/`vault.kv.delete` are `requires_approval=True` (descriptor specs `ops.py:1147-1148`, `:1209-1210`); `secret.move` is `requires_approval=True` + `safety_level="dangerous"` (`connectors/secret/ops.py:259-260`). Safety is enforced by the confirm modal + the dispatcher's `policy_gate` (`operations/_validate.py:141`) → approval queue, NOT by `TenantRole`. Do NOT add a tenant_admin hard-403 on the write POST — that contradicts the backend gate and the operations console. The only tenant_admin-gated surface is `llm_instructions` in any op-detail drawer (soft-hide via `resolve_role_probe`, `ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:152`, fails soft — returns the no-privileges probe at `operator.py:181`). Tenant scoping comes from `operator.tenant_id` only; the default-on vault scope guard (`connectors/vault/tenant_scope.py:143`, raises `VaultTenantScopeError` at `:211`) denies writes outside `secret/tenants/{tenant_id}/` — render that as a clear scope message, not a raw 403.

## Acceptance criteria

- `pytest backend/tests/ -k "vault_ui and put and awaiting"` (new test): a confirmed `POST /ui/vault/put` whose dispatch returns `status="awaiting_approval"` renders the approval banner with `extras["approval_request_id"]` AND a link whose href targets `/ui/approvals` — asserting the operator is NOT shown a silent/empty success.
- New test (confirm gate + CSRF + route order): the `vault.kv.delete` confirm modal renders the `dangerous` / `requires_approval` banner; `POST /ui/vault/delete` without the CSRF token → `403`, with it → `200`; and the literal `GET /ui/vault/put/confirm` resolves to the confirm handler, not any T1 `{param}` route on the shared `/ui/vault` router (first-match-wins — register literals before params).
- New test (CAS): `POST /ui/vault/put` carries `cas` in the dispatched params only when the operator set it; omitting the CAS field dispatches without a `cas` key (mirrors the CLI `Changed("cas")` rule).
- New test (`secret.move` value-free contract): `POST /ui/vault/move` dispatches `connector_id="secret-broker-1.x"` op `secret.move` with `from`/`to` references and NO value field; the rendered result contains only `status` / `value_sha256` / `length` and no secret value text. Assert the move form has no value/secret input.
- New test (RBAC): a valid **operator** session can run all three writes; no tenant_admin hard-403 is asserted on the write POST; tenant scoping is derived from the session, not a form field.
- `cd cli && make snapshot-openapi && make generate` is run and the regenerated `cli/api/openapi.json` + `cli/internal/api/client.gen.go` are committed (the new `/ui/vault/put|delete|move*` routes land in the snapshot; "CLI API snapshot freshness" CI lane enforces it).
- `cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy src/` clean.

## Out of scope

- The KV browser scaffold (picker / list / read / versions) → **T1** (#1942).
- Seal/health/mounts + auth-methods status view → **T3** (#1942).
- Implementing/re-implementing the approval *decide* flow — that lives on `/ui/approvals` (#1778); this task only **deep-links** to it.
- `vault.kv.patch` (no CLI verb surfaces it; out of the planned T-row set).
- Any new backend route, connector op, or meta-tool — BFF + template assembly only.

## References

- Initiative #1942. Sibling Initiative #1835 (G10.9 operations console) — the merged `ui/routes/operations/routes.py` is the canonical confirm-gated in-process-dispatch BFF precedent.
- Backend: `operations/meta_tools.py:1000` (`call_operation`), `operations/_validate.py:141` (`policy_gate`), `operations/_errors.py:251` (`result_awaiting_approval`), `connectors/vault/ops.py:1147-1148` (put descriptor caution/requires_approval), `ops.py:1209-1210` (delete dangerous/requires_approval), `ops.py:563` (`vault_kv_put` handler), `ops.py:898` (`vault_kv_delete` handler), `connectors/secret/ops.py:240,250-260` (`secret.move` registrar/value-free/safety), `connectors/secret/ops.py:87` (`SECRET_MOVE_PARAMETER_SCHEMA`, value-rejection), `connectors/secret/ops.py:171` (`secret_move` handler), `:211-215` (value-free `{status, value_sha256, length}` return), `connectors/vault/tenant_scope.py:143,211`.
- CLI surface (op-id + key-order source of truth): `cli/internal/cmd/vault/kv.go:179-195` (put + `casSet` at `:186`), `kv.go:224-253` (delete cmd), `cli/internal/cmd/secret/secret.go:57` (`const ConnectorID = "secret-broker-1.x"`), `cli/internal/cmd/secret/move.go:18` (`opMove`), `move.go:140` (`moveResultKeyOrder`).
- Precedent surfaces: `ui/routes/operations/routes.py:459-507` (run modal route + call POST), `:776-822` (`_render_run_modal`, CSRF re-mint at `:807`/`:821`), `:825` (`_render_call_result`), `:886` (`_render_call_form_error`), `:211-212` (`mint_csrf_token` / `set_csrf_cookie` imports), `ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:152,181` (soft-hide `llm_instructions`, soft-fail return), `ui/routes/approvals/routes.py:386` (`GET /ui/approvals/{request_id}` deep-link target), `ui/templates/operations/_run_modal.html` + `_result.html` (modal + result fragment shape), `ui/csrf.py:199` (`mint_csrf_token`, double-submit gate).
- Framework anchors (pinned from the checkout): HTMX 2.0.9 (`ui/static/src/vendor/htmx.min.js`) — `hx-post` / `hx-target` / `hx-disabled-elt` (disable confirm during dispatch) / `hx-headers`, https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-disabled-elt/ ; Alpine.js 3.15.12 (`ui/static/src/vendor/VENDOR.md` line 27) — `x-data` for the confirm-modal open state, https://alpinejs.dev/directives/data ; FastAPI `>=0.136.3,<0.137` (`backend/pyproject.toml:14`) `Form` / `APIRouter`; Pydantic v2 `>=2.13.4` (`backend/pyproject.toml:16`); Jinja2 `>=3.1.6` (`backend/pyproject.toml:35`).
