labels.description: Operator web UI — G10.x HTMX/Jinja console surface

items.body:
Parent goal: #336
Parent initiative: #1842

## Context

A tenant admin who watches a PII/secret leak scroll past on the live `/ui/broadcast` feed today has no in-console way to suppress that op's detail — they must drop to the CLI (`meho broadcast overrides set ...`). The durable per-tenant suppression rules already have a complete backend: `BroadcastOverride` rows + the tenant-admin CRUD plane in `backend/src/meho_backplane/api/v1/broadcast_overrides.py` (G6.3-T4 #381, CLOSED, under Initiative #376). This task adds a third tab — **Overrides** — to the existing `/ui/broadcast` Alpine tab strip so a tenant admin can list, create, and delete those rules without leaving the console.

A broadcast override sets the published detail level for ops matching `op_id_pattern` (a **glob**, not regex) to either `full` or `aggregate`. The sensitive op-classes (`credential_read` / `credential_mint` / `audit_query` — the "aggregate-only per decision #3" set documented at `feed.py:98-100`) already render aggregate-only on the feed; an override is how a tenant admin pins suppression for any op-id they choose, or (the footgun) **re-exposes** previously-suppressed detail by deleting a rule.

## Current state (grounded against HEAD `7acae0d1`)

- The broadcast surface is a four-module router aggregated in `ui/routes/broadcast/__init__.py` → `build_router()` (`__init__.py:60-81`): feed (`/ui/broadcast` + `/ui/broadcast/feed`), stream (`/ui/broadcast/stream`), history (`/ui/broadcast/history`), event (`/ui/broadcast/event/{audit_id}`). The literal fragment routers are deliberately included **before** the parametrised event router (`__init__.py:68-80`, "declaration order is the contract FastAPI resolves on").
- The tab strip lives in `templates/broadcast/feed.html:77-100`: an Alpine `x-data="{ tab: 'live' }"` (line 77) with two `role="tab"` buttons (Live / Last 24h). The Last-24h pane lazy-loads via `hx-get="/ui/broadcast/history" hx-trigger="intersect once"` (`feed.html:127-129`). This is the exact lazy-load pattern the Overrides pane should mirror (note the tab values are `'live'` / `'history'`; the new pane is `'overrides'`).
- Backend CRUD (`api/v1/broadcast_overrides.py`), router prefix `/api/v1/broadcast/overrides`, every route gated by `Depends(require_role(TenantRole.TENANT_ADMIN))` (built once as `_require_tenant_admin`, line 132):
  - `GET /api/v1/broadcast/overrides` → `list_overrides` (line 391) → `list_overrides_impl` (line 258); tenant-scoped at the first `WHERE BroadcastOverride.tenant_id == operator.tenant_id` (line 274-276).
  - `POST /api/v1/broadcast/overrides` → `create_override` (line 440, **status 201**) → `create_override_impl` (line 284); `IntegrityError` on the composite-unique index → **409** `broadcast_override_already_exists` (line 331-334).
  - `DELETE /api/v1/broadcast/overrides/{override_id}` → `delete_override` (line 453, status 204) → `delete_override_impl` (line 349); cross-tenant id → **404** `broadcast_override_not_found` (line 377-380) — never 403, existence is not leaked across tenants.
  - Request schema `BroadcastOverrideCreate` (line 140): `op_id_pattern` (1–128 chars), `scope_field: Literal["namespace","target_name"] | None`, `scope_value: str | None` (max 128), `detail: Literal["full","aggregate"]`. `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` (line 156). Two `model_validator(mode="after")`: scope_field/scope_value must both be set or both be NULL (line 163-169); `op_id_pattern` rejects regex-like chars `_REGEX_LIKE_CHARS = frozenset("[](){}\\+?|^$")` (line 125) → **422** with message `op_id_pattern must be glob, not regex; rejected chars: [...]` (line 171-178). The list response model is `BroadcastOverrideRead` (line 181) carrying `created_by_sub` + `created_at` + `updated_at`.
- There is **no** `/ui/broadcast/overrides*` route and no overrides template today.
- RBAC lift helpers exist and must be reused (`ui/routes/connectors/operator.py`): `resolve_role_probe` (line 152 — soft-hide, returns `OperatorRoleProbe(is_tenant_admin, is_operator)`, fails soft to no-privileges on any JWT hiccup) and `resolve_operator_or_403` (line 184 — lifts the full `Operator` via `_lift_operator` (line 135) and raises **403** if `tenant_role != TenantRole.TENANT_ADMIN`).
- CSRF: `ui/csrf.py` — every state-changing `/ui/*` request needs the double-submit token via `X-CSRF-Token` (HTMX `hx-headers` on `<body>`) or the `csrf_token` form field; the token is minted with `mint_csrf_token(str(session_ctx.session_id))` and the `meho_csrf` cookie set on the GET render (see `feed.py:_render_page` line 243, `mint_csrf_token` line 274 + `set_cookie` line 291).

## Scope

Add an **Overrides** tab to `/ui/broadcast`, server-rendered + HTMX, going through the in-process BFF (session cookie + `require_ui_session`), **not** the Bearer API. New routes under a new module `ui/routes/broadcast/overrides.py`, aggregated into `build_router()`:

1. **`GET /ui/broadcast/overrides`** — the tab's lazy-loaded fragment (`templates/broadcast/_overrides.html`, no chrome). Renders the tenant's rules as a table: `op_id_pattern`, scope (`scope_field=scope_value` or "op-wide"), `detail` badge (`full` vs `aggregate`), `created_by_sub`, `created_at`. Above the table, a banner explaining **most-specific-wins resolution** — a scoped rule (`scope_field`/`scope_value` set) beats an op-wide rule for the same pattern — so a flat table is not misread as flat-priority. The fragment must be **tenant_admin-gated**: use `resolve_operator_or_403` so a non-admin operator gets a 403-driven "Overrides require tenant_admin" empty state rather than the table; **do not query the DB directly** — call the backend `list_overrides_impl` with the lifted `Operator` + a `get_session` session so the UI never diverges from the API's RBAC contract.
2. **Create affordance** — a form (modal or inline, mirror `templates/memory/_create_modal.html:68-72`'s `hx-post`/`hx-target="this"`/`hx-disabled-elt="find button[type=submit]"` shape) that `hx-post`s to `POST /ui/broadcast/overrides`. Fields: `op_id_pattern` (text, hint "glob only — `*` and literals; no regex"), `scope_field` (select: op-wide / namespace / target_name), `scope_value` (text, shown when a scope_field is chosen), `detail` (select: full / aggregate). The handler calls `create_override_impl`; on success it `hx-swap`s the refreshed table in (re-render the fragment). Echo the backend's **422 glob-not-regex** validation and the **409 already-exists** as inline form errors (read `detail` off the response) — do not silently no-op.
3. **Delete-with-consequence** — each row's delete is a two-step confirm, **not** a one-click row action. The confirm modal (DaisyUI `<dialog>`, mirror `templates/memory/detail.html:147-167`) must spell out the consequence in prose: *"Deleting this rule re-exposes the suppressed detail for matching ops on the live feed and the Slack mirror."* The confirm button `hx-delete`s `/ui/broadcast/overrides/{override_id}`; on 204 re-render the table; surface a 404 as "rule already removed".
4. **"Suppress this op" cross-link** — on the feed/history event rows and/or the event-detail drawer, add a link from **sensitive** rows (rows whose `op_class` is in the aggregate-only sensitive set — `credential_read` / `credential_mint` / `audit_query`, documented at `feed.py:98-100`; note that of these only `credential_read`/`credential_mint` carry the `badge-warning` class while `audit_query` is `badge-info` per `OP_CLASS_BADGE_CLASSES`, so gate the cross-link on the sensitive *set*, not on the badge colour) into the Overrides tab with the row's `op_id` pre-filled into the create form's `op_id_pattern`. The cross-link is a UX shortcut; the create still goes through the same gated POST.

The new tab button + pane wire into the existing `feed.html` Alpine `x-data="{ tab: 'live' }"` strip (add a third `tab === 'overrides'` pane that lazy-loads `GET /ui/broadcast/overrides` on first activation, exactly like the history pane's `intersect once` at `feed.html:127-129`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `GET /ui/broadcast/overrides` as a **tenant_admin** returns 200 with a table of that tenant's rules; as a non-admin operator it returns 403 (or renders the gated empty state) and never the table — assert both in `tests/.../ui/routes/broadcast/test_overrides.py::test_overrides_tab_tenant_admin_gated`, using the `resolve_operator_or_403` lift, mirroring the connectors probe RBAC test.
2. `POST /ui/broadcast/overrides` with a regex-bearing `op_id_pattern` (e.g. `k8s.(get|list)`) surfaces the backend **422 glob-not-regex** message inline (not a 500, not a blank success); a duplicate `(tenant_id, op_id_pattern, scope_field, scope_value)` surfaces the **409 `broadcast_override_already_exists`** message — assert both via `TestClient` against the UI route with a valid CSRF token (`test_overrides_create_surfaces_422_and_409`).
3. The delete confirm modal body text contains the literal re-exposure warning (feed + Slack mirror) — assert `assert "re-expose" in html.lower()` (or the exact warning string) against the rendered `_overrides.html`; a `DELETE /ui/broadcast/overrides/{override_id}` for a cross-tenant override id returns **404, not 403** (`test_overrides_delete_cross_tenant_404`).
4. Every UI mutation (`POST` create, `DELETE`) carries the CSRF double-submit token (`X-CSRF-Token` header inherited from `<body hx-headers>` or `csrf_token` form field); a request missing it gets the `csrf_token_invalid` 403 — assert one CSRF-missing rejection (`test_overrides_mutation_requires_csrf`).
5. The Overrides router module is included in `ui/routes/broadcast/__init__.py:build_router()` **before** `build_event_router()`, keeping the literal `/ui/broadcast/overrides` ahead of the parametrised `/ui/broadcast/event/{audit_id}` per the file's documented declaration-order discipline — assert `GET /ui/broadcast/overrides` resolves to the overrides handler (not the event handler) in the test.
6. Because new `/ui/*` routes are added, run `cd cli && make snapshot-openapi && make generate` and commit the regenerated `cli/api/openapi.json` (it will gain `/ui/broadcast/overrides` and `/ui/broadcast/overrides/{override_id}`) + `cli/internal/api/client.gen.go`; CI lane "CLI API snapshot freshness" enforces this. Verify locally with `git diff --name-only` showing both files staged and the new paths present in `cli/api/openapi.json`.

## Out of scope

- Editing a rule in place (the backend has no PATCH; delete + recreate is the model). Do not add a UI edit verb.
- Any change to override **resolution** semantics, the per-tenant cache (`invalidate_tenant_cache`), or the publish-time transport (G6.3-T2/T3 — backend, complete).
- A standalone `/ui/overrides` sidebar surface — this is a tab on the existing broadcast surface, no new sidebar entry.
- Bulk import/export of rules.

## References

- Backend CRUD: `backend/src/meho_backplane/api/v1/broadcast_overrides.py` — router prefix `/api/v1/broadcast/overrides` (line 106), `_require_tenant_admin` gate (line 132), `BroadcastOverrideCreate` (line 140), `_REGEX_LIKE_CHARS` (line 125), `BroadcastOverrideRead` (line 181), `list_overrides_impl` (line 258), `create_override_impl` (line 284; 409 path line 331), `delete_override_impl` (line 349; 404 path line 377), route handlers `list_overrides`/`create_override`/`delete_override` (lines 391/440/453).
- Tab strip + lazy-load precedent: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/templates/broadcast/feed.html:77-100` (Alpine `x-data` tabs) + `:127-129` (history pane `hx-get`/`hx-trigger="intersect once"`).
- Router aggregation + literal-before-param ordering: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/routes/broadcast/__init__.py:60-81` (discipline documented at 68-80).
- RBAC lift (reuse, do not re-implement): `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/routes/connectors/operator.py` — `_lift_operator` (line 135), `resolve_role_probe` (line 152), `resolve_operator_or_403` (line 184, 403 path line 199-203).
- CSRF + cookie/token mint precedent: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/csrf.py`; `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/routes/broadcast/feed.py:243` (`_render_page`), line 274 (`mint_csrf_token`) + line 291 (`set_cookie`).
- Delete-confirm `<dialog>` modal precedent: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/templates/memory/detail.html:147-167`. Create-modal `hx-post`/`hx-disabled-elt` precedent: `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/templates/memory/_create_modal.html:68-72`.
- Sensitive op_class set (the cross-link trigger): `backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/routes/broadcast/feed.py:98-115` (`OP_CLASS_BADGE_CLASSES` — `credential_read`/`credential_mint` = `badge-warning`, `audit_query` = `badge-info`; the three are the aggregate-only sensitive set per decision #3).
- Frameworks (pinned from repo): FastAPI `>=0.136.3,<0.137` (`backend/pyproject.toml:14`), Jinja2 `>=3.1.6` (`:35`), Pydantic `>=2.13.4` (`:16`); vendored HTMX 2.0.9 + SSE ext + Alpine 3.15.12 (`backend/src/meho_backplane/ui/static/src/vendor/{htmx,sse,alpine}.min.js`, wired in `ui/templates/_head_assets.html:35-37`). HTMX attrs: https://htmx.org/reference/ ; DaisyUI modal `<dialog>`: https://daisyui.com/components/modal/

items.title: match_related attribute of class DeploymentEventTrigger doesn't accept the type List[Dict], but the docs suggest it should
items.body:
### Bug summary


I am using the Python Class to write and configure my deployments. I noticed a mismatch between what's doable in python and what seems to be doable with YAML/JSON. Given the documentation [here](https://docs.prefect.io/v3/concepts/event-triggers#example), specially this section:

"""
match_related also supports an array of objects, each of which can contain multiple labels. This allows for more complex matching on related resources, such as filtering for events that are related to a specific work pool or tag.
"""

However, the python class only accept for the input `match_related` the class `ResourceSpecification`, which itself only takes one argument, root, and is of type `Dict[str, str | List[str]]` (Subclass of pydantic RootModel)

Then, it is impossible to configure a rule that will need to match all tag of a set of tags to fire. The possible list, value of the root dictionnary, seems to be a logical OR between all elements that compose the list, according to what I have tested.

### Version info

```Text
## Environment

prefect-server: 3.6.19
postgres backend, v18
self hosted docker setup
reproduced on arch linux
```

### Additional context


I'm building a multi-tenant event driven ELT pipeline. I want to fire subset of computation in [dbt](https://www.getdbt.com) based on tags, with tags defined in prefect matching tags defined in dbt, all targeting the same conceptual component. I have defined my own event grammar for this use case.

Here's the deployer I'm using:
```python
DeploymentEventTrigger(
    name=f"dbt-reactive-{provider}-{tenant_name.lower()}",
    description=f"Trigger on {chosen_threshold_value} {provider} events",
    type="event",
    posture=Posture.Reactive,
    expect={f"elt.{provider}.*"},
    for_each={f"prefect.resource.id"},
    threshold=chosen_threshold_value,
    within=timedelta(seconds=1200),
    match=ResourceSpecification(
        {"prefect.resource.id": f"elt.{provider}.*"}
    ),
    match_related=ResourceSpecification(
        {"prefect.resource.id": [f"prefect.tag.bronze", f"prefect.tag.{tenant_name.lower()}"]},
    ),
    parameters={
        "tenant_id": tenant_id,
        "config": {
            "commands": ["seed", "snapshot", "run"],
            "selects": [f"+tag:{provider}+"],
        }
    },
    schedule_after=timedelta(
        minutes=20
)
```

This trigger is part of a for loop, each provider being an independent source of data. The objective is, when sufficient amount of bronze-flows-events for that specific provider and that specific tenant are emitted, I fire the trigger. Currently, it's not working, a tenant A can fire the trigger for an tenant B, because the list is a treated as a OR. If I can define the following:
```python
match_related = [
    {"prefect.resource.id": "prefect.tag.bronze"},
    {"prefect.resource.id": f"prefect.tag.{provider}"},
]
```
The problem should disappear.

I'm probably doing something wrong here, following some anti-pattern. Although I'd appreciate some help for this, the main point is to give some context on why I would need this and to point out the mismatch between the doc and the python implementation.

Switching to yaml is not really an option, as I define these triggers dynamically based on my database. I don't really want to glue code something with jinja, specially when prefect propose the wonderful feature to write IaC in python.

Happy to provide additional information!

items.title: Task: Operator console: connector ingest modal (catalog or explicit-quadruple) with dry-run + async job-poll

labels.name: frontend
labels.description: Operator web UI — G10.x HTMX/Jinja console surface

items.body:
Parent goal: #336
Parent initiative: #1839

## Context

Ingesting a vendor OpenAPI spec into the connector registry is CLI/MCP-only today. This Task adds the **ingest modal** to the console: an operator picks a catalog entry (or supplies an explicit `product`/`version`/`impl_id`/`specs[]` quadruple), optionally **dry-runs** the parse, then kicks off a real ingest and **watches the async job poll to completion** — all from `/ui/connectors/registry` (T1).

The ingest backend is fully shipped. The async path is the load-bearing part: on a real vendor spec the pipeline blocks its worker (~tens of seconds) and the job lives in **process-local** memory that evaporates on pod restart (initiative grounding note: "Async ingest is process-local"; `jobs.py:20` — "Storage is process-local"). The poll UI must degrade gracefully — a 404 after restart means "job lost, re-check the registry list," never an infinite spinner.

### Backend surface to reuse (all opened + line-verified at HEAD `7acae0d1`)

- `api/v1/connectors_ingest.py:308` — `POST /api/v1/connectors/ingest` (`ingest_endpoint`, `connectors_ingest.py:344`, gated by `_require_admin` = `TENANT_ADMIN`, `:346`). Two response shapes are declared in the `responses=` map: **202 + `IngestJobHandle`** (async default) or **200 + `IngestResponse`** (sync, used for `dry_run` and `async=false`). The route branches: `dry_run or not async_` → `_run_sync_ingest` (`:448`); else → `_spawn_async_ingest` (`:484`).
- `operations/ingest/api_schemas.py` — `IngestRequest` (`product`/`version`/`impl_id` fields at `:180-182`). **Two mutually-exclusive shapes** enforced by the `_exactly_one_request_shape` validator (`api_schemas.py:~250-300`): catalog-driven (`catalog_entry="<product>/<version>"`, every quadruple field empty) **or** explicit-quadruple (`product`+`version`+`impl_id`+`specs[]`, `catalog_entry` unset). Mixing → 422 `catalog_entry_conflict`; omitting both → 422 underspecified. `async_` is aliased to `async` on the wire; `dry_run` defaults False. `specs[]` is a list of `SpecSource{uri, content}`.
- `operations/ingest/api_schemas.py:713` — `IngestJobHandle{job_id: UUID, status, poll_url}`. `:738` — `IngestJobStatusResponse{job_id, status, catalog_entry, product, version, impl_id, spec_uris, started_at, ended_at, ingestion: IngestionResultModel|None, grouping: GroupingResultModel|None, error, error_class}`. Status literal `IngestJobStatusLiteral = Literal["running","succeeded","failed","degraded"]` at `:710`. **`degraded`** is terminal-but-not-green (pipeline ran, nothing dispatchable landed) and carries the structured `error_class="ingested_not_dispatchable"` (`api_schemas.py:706-709`; the job-registry flip is `IngestJobRegistry.mark_degraded`, `jobs.py:238-258`).
- `api/v1/connectors_ingest.py:610` — `GET /api/v1/connectors/ingest/jobs/{job_id}` (`get_ingest_job_endpoint`, `_require_admin` = `TENANT_ADMIN`, `:612`). **Process-local**: a poll against a freshly-restarted pod returns **404 `ingest_job_not_found`** (`IngestJobRegistry.get`, `jobs.py:297`); cross-tenant/built-in probes 404 the same way (`jobs.py:311`).
- `api/v1/connectors_ingest.py:1101` — `GET /api/v1/connectors/catalog` (`catalog_endpoint`, `_require_operator` = `OPERATOR`, `:1102`) → `CatalogListResponse`. Drives the catalog picker dropdown.
- Catalog-resolution 422s the modal must render (`connectors_ingest.py:687-832`): `catalog_entry_malformed`, `catalog_entry_not_found` (with `available_entries[]`, built at `:740` from `f"{e.product}/{e.version}"`), `catalog_entry_typed_connector`, `catalog_entry_templated_upstream` (operator must fall back to the explicit-quadruple shape). Plus the ingest domain errors mapped at `connectors_ingest.py:968-1057`: `LlmClientUnavailable` → **503** (`:987`), `VersionMismatchError`/`ProductImplIdMismatch`/`UncoveredVersionLabel` → **422**, the `400` spec-parse family.

### Precedent UI surface

- `ui/templates/agents/runs/_status_panel.html` — **the async-poll pattern.** While the run is non-terminal the wrapper carries `hx-get="/ui/agents/runs/{{ run.run_id }}"` + `hx-trigger="every {{ poll_interval_seconds }}s"` + `hx-swap="outerHTML"` (`_status_panel.html:27-29`); once terminal it **drops** those directives so the poll cycle ends naturally (the "stop returning the polling element" idiom, documented in the template at `:11-16`, https://htmx.org/docs/#polling). No JS, no 286-response plumbing. **Model the job-poll fragment on this.**
- `ui/routes/connectors/import_view.py` — the paste→preview→confirm modal flow (stateless: server holds no plan between requests; re-validates on confirm). CSRF cookie mint at `import_view.py:412` (`render_import_page`) + `_set_csrf_cookie` (`:349`); the inline-error-422 fragment is `_render_inline_error` (`import_view.py:361`, returns `status_code=422`).
- `ui/routes/connectors/forms_router.py:75-127` — the create-modal handlers (`_create_modal_handler`/`_create_submit_handler`) showing the in-process-BFF-calls-REST pattern; call `ingest_endpoint` in-process, do not go through the Bearer route.
- `ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:184` — `resolve_operator_or_403` (the write gate; ingest is `TENANT_ADMIN`). `ui/csrf.py:199` — `mint_csrf_token`.
- `ui/routes/connectors/__init__.py:79,88-112` — first-match-wins registration-order commentary.

## Scope

Add the ingest modal + job-poll surface, reachable from the T1 registry list:

1. **Ingest modal** — `GET /ui/connectors/registry/ingest` returns an HTMX-loaded `<dialog class="modal">` fragment (shared `modal-dialogs.js` container, `base.html:101-112`). Two tabs/modes: **catalog** (a dropdown populated by calling `catalog_endpoint` in-process) and **explicit quadruple** (`product`/`version`/`impl_id` text inputs + one-or-more `specs[].uri` rows; inline `specs[].content` byte upload is out of scope — the UI uses `https://` URIs only). A **Dry-run** checkbox/button. Write RBAC = **TENANT_ADMIN** via `resolve_operator_or_403`; soft-hide the "Ingest" entry point from non-admins on T1's list.
2. **Submit handler** — `POST /ui/connectors/registry/ingest` builds an `IngestRequest` from the form (exactly one shape — never set both `catalog_entry` and quadruple fields; let `_exactly_one_request_shape` be the authority but pre-check in the handler to render a friendly inline error rather than a raw 422) and calls `ingest_endpoint` **in-process**. Branch on the response:
   - **Dry-run** (`dry_run=true`) → 200 `IngestResponse`; render the parse counts inline in the modal, write nothing.
   - **Real async** (`dry_run=false`, default) → 202 `IngestJobHandle`; render the **job-poll fragment** seeded with `job_id`.
3. **Job-poll fragment + route** — `GET /ui/connectors/registry/ingest/jobs/{job_id}` (`TENANT_ADMIN` via `resolve_operator_or_403`, mirroring the REST `_require_admin` gate) calls `get_ingest_job_endpoint` in-process and renders `_ingest_job_status.html`. While `status == "running"` the fragment self-polls via `hx-trigger="every Ns"` (the `_status_panel.html` idiom); on a terminal status it drops the poll directive. Terminal rendering:
   - `succeeded` → counts + a refresh/link to the T1 registry list (and the "Review" entry point for T3).
   - `degraded` → show the counts **and** the `error_class="ingested_not_dispatchable"` reason (`error` message) — not a green success.
   - `failed` → show `error_class` + `error`.
   - **404 on poll** → render a "job lost (the pod may have restarted) — re-check the registry list" panel and stop polling. Do **not** spin forever.
4. **Error rendering** — the catalog-resolution 422s (with `available_entries[]` for `catalog_entry_not_found`), the explicit-shape 422s (`VersionMismatchError`/`ProductImplIdMismatch`/`UncoveredVersionLabel`), the `400` spec-parse family, and `503 LlmClientUnavailable` all render as actionable inline modal panels (initiative footgun: render 503/409 as actionable panels).

## Acceptance criteria

- A pytest (`tests/unit/ui/routes/connectors/test_registry_ingest.py::test_dry_run_writes_nothing`) drives the modal submit in **dry-run** mode and asserts the response is the 200 sync-shape render (parse counts present) and that `get_job_registry()` gained **no** job row (nothing written).
- A pytest drives a **real async** submit and asserts a 202-shaped render containing the `job_id` and a poll fragment whose root element carries `hx-trigger="every`; a follow-up flips the seeded job terminal and asserts the re-rendered fragment **omits** `hx-trigger` (poll stops) — pins the "stop returning the polling element" contract.
- A pytest asserts a poll for an **unknown job_id** renders the "job lost — re-check the registry list" panel (driven by the in-process 404 from `IngestJobRegistry.get`) and the fragment carries **no** `hx-trigger` (no infinite spinner) — guards the process-local-jobs footgun.
- A pytest asserts a `degraded` job renders both the ingestion counts **and** the `ingested_not_dispatchable` reason (not a bare success); and a `catalog_entry_not_found` 422 renders an inline panel listing `available_entries[]`, and a `503 LlmClientUnavailable` renders an actionable panel (not a 500).
- A pytest asserts the ingest submit + the poll route require TENANT_ADMIN (403 for an operator) and CSRF double-submit on the POST (missing `X-CSRF-Token` rejected by `CSRFMiddleware`).
- A pytest asserts a body that sets **both** `catalog_entry` and a quadruple field is rejected with a friendly inline error (handler pre-check or the `catalog_entry_conflict` validator), not a 500.
- **OpenAPI snapshot**: this Task adds new `/ui/connectors/registry/ingest*` routes, so run `cd cli && make snapshot-openapi && make generate` and commit `cli/api/openapi.json` + `cli/internal/api/client.gen.go`; "CLI API snapshot freshness" CI lane green. A route-ordering pytest asserts the new literal `/ui/connectors/registry/ingest*` routes register **before** `/ui/connectors/{name}` (first-match-wins).

## Out of scope

- The registry list itself + per-row enable/disable/delete (T1, #1839) — this Task depends on T1's surface existing.
- The review drawer (T3, #1839).
- Inline `specs[].content` byte upload (CLI-only on-ramp); built-in/global-scope ingest via the optional MCP `tenant_id`.
- Durable cross-restart jobs (a documented backend follow-up, `jobs.py:20`) — the UI accepts the process-local trade and degrades gracefully.

## References

- Backend: `api/v1/connectors_ingest.py:308,344,448,484` (ingest), `:610,612` (job poll), `:1101` (catalog), `:687-832` (catalog-resolution 422s), `:968-1057` (domain-error map); `operations/ingest/api_schemas.py:180-182,706-710,713,738`; `operations/ingest/jobs.py:20,238-258,297,311`.
- Precedent UI: `ui/templates/agents/runs/_status_panel.html:11-29`, `ui/routes/connectors/import_view.py:349,361,412`, `ui/routes/connectors/forms_router.py:75-127`, `ui/routes/connectors/operator.py:184`, `ui/csrf.py:199`, `ui/templates/base.html:101-112`.
- HTMX (vendored): polling / "stop returning the polling element" (https://htmx.org/docs/#polling), `hx-trigger="every Ns"` (https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-trigger/), `hx-disabled-elt` on the submit button (precedent: `ui/templates/connectors/_edit_modal.html`).
- Pydantic v2 / FastAPI / Jinja2 per `backend/pyproject.toml`.

Depends-on: #1885

items.title: Write the reference quadrant from what the code exposes
items.body:
**Category**: feature | **Scope**: Large

## Description

This issue fills the reference quadrant of the site #105 stood up (PR #112) and #106 filled on the explanation side (PR #113): 23 pages under `docs/reference/` in five collapsed sidebar groups (Reporting API, command lines, configuration, schemas and formats, observability), plus a Go package `internal/refdoc` that renders the parts of a page the code decides and tests that fail `go test ./...` when a rendered part no longer matches the page. The vertical slice's readme is folded into that program's page and deleted, the five explanation pages that name the reference quadrant in plain text gain their links, and the reference index lists every surface.

Two decisions by the author (2026-09-06) bound the work. First, the quadrant takes every contract the seven monographs hold, not only the surfaces the issue lists: the clouds file and the counter sources file, the pricing adjustments schema, the OpenStack notification mapping and the size bounds of refused events, the scrape jobs and the Alertmanager routing of the base manifests, and the simulator's control endpoint, fake OpenStack API, file formats and fault switches. The description of the generated simulator world (`docs/openstack-simulator.md` lines 29 to 479) stays out as generator design. #108 removes a monograph only when every part has a home, so this is what lets it remove all seven. Second, the dev-cluster drill of `cmd/tally-vertical-slice/README.md` (lines 45 to 198) is dropped: the page carries the contract and the golden document, `cmd/tally-vertical-slice/slice_integration_test.go` holds the numbers in CI, and the cluster steps are lesson one of #109.

Assumption, per #106: GitHub Pages is not enabled yet and the published root is `https://b42labs.github.io/tally/`; the one link written outside the site (`docs/drills/phase3.md` line 32) answers 404 until the admin call quoted in `.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yaml` runs.

### 1. The scaffold exists; this issue fills the reference quadrant

### 2. Generated blocks inside hand-written pages, checked by tests

Already exists: the pattern. `internal/reporting/httpapi/spec_test.go` (`TestEmbeddedSpecMatchesTheDocument`) compares a generated artifact with its source and fails with "run `make generate`"; `make generate` (Makefile line 292) runs the generators and the output is committed; `internal/core/testkit` is a non-test package tests import. The renderers' dependencies are direct requirements in `go.mod` already (`kin-openapi`, `cobra`, `client_golang`, `yaml.v3`); reading gathered families needs `github.com/prometheus/client_model/go`, which `go mod tidy` moves from the indirect block without adding a module.

This issue adds the package `internal/refdoc`; the exported surface below is the contract, the file split is the implementer's.

A generated block is the text between two marker lines:

```markdown
<!-- refdoc:begin settings -->
(rendered text)
<!-- refdoc:end settings -->
```

The name matches `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, is unique within the page, and the end marker repeats it. Text outside the markers is hand-written; text between them is replaced wholesale, ends with a newline, and the markers stand on their own lines.

Type words, used wherever a renderer names a Go or pflag type: `string` string; `bool` boolean; `int`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint64` integer; `float64` number; `duration` duration; `[]string` and pflag `stringSlice` "list, comma-separated"; pflag `stringArray` "string, repeatable"; `time.Time` "string, RFC 3339 UTC"; `money.Amount` "decimal, 2 places"; `money.Quantity`, `jsonMinutes`, `jsonQuantity` "decimal, 4 places"; `money.Rate` "decimal, 6 places"; `json.RawMessage` and `map[string]any` object; `*T` "T or null"; `[]T` "array of T"; `map[string]T` "object of T"; a named type rendered in the same call a link to its heading (`[Document](#document)`); anything else verbatim in a code span.

Exported surface:

- `Verify(t testing.TB, page string, blocks map[string]string)`: for every name in the map it reads the page, extracts the block and compares. A mismatch fails with `t.Errorf` naming the page, the block and the line `run make generate`, then the first 20 differing lines as want and got. With the environment variable `TALLY_UPDATE_DOCS` set to `1` it rewrites every mismatching block in place and fails nothing. A missing page fails with `t.Fatalf` naming the path and the `fs.ErrNotExist` error. Errors: `%s: no block %q (add the markers)`, `%s: block %q is not terminated`, `%s: block %q appears twice`; an empty map is `t.Fatalf("%s: Verify called with no blocks", page)`.
- `Fenced(lang string, body []byte) string`: a fenced block whose fence is one backtick longer than the longest backtick run in the body; an empty or nil body renders an empty fenced block.
- `Commands(root *cobra.Command) (string, error)`: depth-first over every command `IsAvailableCommand()` reports that is named neither `help` nor `completion`: an H3 heading holding the command path plus the argument part of `Use` in a code span (`` ### `tally-engine migrate-down-to <version>` ``), `Short`, `Long` when it differs, `UseLine()` fenced, a table Subcommand, Purpose when it has subcommands, and a table Flag, Type, Default, Required, Description of its local flags, else "This command takes no flags." Required is "yes" when the annotations carry `cobra.BashCompOneRequiredFlag`; Type is `pflag.Value.Type()` as a type word; Default is `DefValue`, or none for `""` and `[]`; a flag named `help` is skipped. Nil root: `refdoc: nil command`.
- `Flags(fs *flag.FlagSet) (string, error)`: the same table without Required, the type from `flag.UnquoteUsage`, in `VisitAll` order; an empty set renders "This program takes no flags."; nil is `refdoc: nil flag set`.
- `Settings(src []byte, structName string, envNames []string) (string, error)`: parses one Go file (`go/parser`, `parser.ParseComments`), finds `structName`, renders one row per `env`-tagged field in field order: Variable (the tag value), Type (a type word; outside `string`, `bool`, `int`, `int32`, `int64`, `[]string` it is `refdoc: %s.%s: unsupported type %s`), Default (`envDefault`, or none), File-backed ("yes" with `<variable>_FILE` when that name is in `envNames`, else "no"), Governs (the doc comment, lines joined by one space). Errors: `refdoc: %s.%s has no doc comment`, `refdoc: %s carries no env-tagged field`, `refdoc: no type %s in the source`, the `go/parser` error with its position.
- `Struct(src []byte, tagKey string, typeNames ...string) (string, error)`: per name in order, an H4 heading with the type name in a code span, its doc comment, and a table Member, Type, Presence, Description; Member is the `tagKey` (`json` or `yaml`) value before the first comma, an untagged field or `-` is skipped; Type a type word; Presence "always", or "omitted when empty" with `omitempty`; Description the field's doc comment, empty when none. Errors: `refdoc: no types named`, `refdoc: no type %s in the source`, `refdoc: %s is not a struct`.
- `Consts(src []byte, names ...string) (string, error)`: a table Name, Value, Meaning for the named constants in order, identifier and literal (a string literal without its quotes) in code spans, the doc comment as Meaning. Errors: `refdoc: no constants named`, `refdoc: no constant %s in the source`.
- `MappingTable(src []byte) (string, error)`: finds the literal assigned to `mappings` in `internal/providers/openstack/mapping.go` and renders one row per key in literal order: oslo event type, Tally event type, Resource type (the key, `eventType`, `resourceType`), State and Size (the `state` and `size` expressions as written, in code spans, or none), Resource id (`resourceIDPath` joined by `.`, then " or " and `resourceIDFallbackPath` when present), Project id (`projectIDPath` joined by `.`, or "request context"), Skipped when (the `skip` expression or none). Errors: `refdoc: mappings[%s]: %s is not a string literal`, `refdoc: no mappings literal in the source`.
- `JSONSchema(schema []byte) (string, error)`: decodes a draft 2020-12 document, renders its `title` and `type`, then one H4 heading per schema object in a code span, the root as `root` and every `$defs` entry in key order. An object with `properties` gets a table Property, Type, Required, Constraints (`enum`, `const`, `pattern`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minimum`, `minItems`, `minProperties`, a link for a `$ref`); one without (`price` in the pricing schema) gets one sentence stating its type or alternatives with their constraints. `additionalProperties` renders as "No other property is allowed.", "Other properties are allowed." or "Other properties are `<type or link>`."; `oneOf` as a bulleted list of the alternatives' `required` and `const` members. Errors: the `*json.SyntaxError` with its offset, `refdoc: schema has no type`, `refdoc: unsupported $ref %q` outside `#/$defs/`.
- `OpenAPISecurity`, `OpenAPIOperations`, `OpenAPISchemas`, each `(doc *openapi3.T) (string, error)`. Security: a table Scheme, Type, Description in name order. Operations: per path in `doc.Paths.InMatchingOrder()` and per method in the order GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, an H3 heading holding method and path template in one code span (`` ### `GET /api/v1/events` ``, which keeps a template ending in `{cloud}` out of VitePress's heading-attribute syntax), the summary, the description, "Security: `<scheme>`" or "No credential.", a table Name, In, Required, Type, Description of parameters (references resolved by the loader), one sentence naming the request body's media type and schema linked as `/reference/api/reporting-api-schemas#eventinput`, and a table Status, Description, Body of responses (Body a schema link, `application/problem+json` for a `Problem`, or none). Schemas: per component schema in name order an H3 heading with its name, its description, and a table Property, Type, Required, Description (a `$ref` a link, an array "array of <type or link>", an enum its values in code spans, `format` or `pattern` after a comma, a property without `type` "any"). Errors: `refdoc: nil document`, `refdoc: the document declares no paths`.
- `Metrics(reg *prometheus.Registry) (string, error)`: a table Metric, Type, Labels, Help for every descriptor `reg.Describe` yields whose name starts with `tally_`, sorted by name; name, help and variable labels parsed from `(*prometheus.Desc).String()`, whose `client_golang` v1.24.1 format is `Desc{fqName: %q, help: %q, unit: %q, constLabels: {%s}, variableLabels: {%s}}` (another shape is `refdoc: cannot parse descriptor %q`); Type from `reg.Gather()` where the family is gathered, else counter for a name ending in `_total` and gauge otherwise, a gathered type contradicting that rule being `refdoc: %s is a %s but its name says %s`. Errors: `refdoc: the registry carries no tally_ metric`, `refdoc: gathering: %w`.
- `AlertRules(rules []byte) (string, error)`: decodes the `groups` shape `deploy/kubernetes/base/vmalert/rules_test.go` decodes; per group "Group `<name>`, evaluated every `<interval>`.", then per rule in file order an H3 heading with the alert or record name in a code span, a table with the rows Severity, For, Runbook for an alerting rule (Runbook the annotation value in a code span or none; For none when absent), the summary in a fenced `text` block and the expression in a fenced `promql` block (the fences keep `{{ $labels.cloud }}` from Vue); a recording rule renders "Recorded series." instead of the table. Errors: the `yaml.v3` error, `refdoc: no groups`, `refdoc: rule %d of group %s has no name`.
- `AlertRouting(cfg []byte) (string, error)`: a table with the rows Receiver, Group by, Group wait, Group interval, Repeat interval of the root route, a table Matchers, Overrides with one row per child route, and one sentence naming the receivers and that none carries an integration when no receiver has a `*_configs` member. Error: `refdoc: no route`.
- `ScrapeJobs(cfg []byte) (string, error)`: a table Job, Interval, Timeout, Targets, Static labels; Targets the `static_configs` targets joined by commas, or "discovered, role `<role>`, kept by `<regex>`" from the first `keep` rule of a `kubernetes_sd_configs` job; Static labels `key=value` pairs in key order or none; Timeout none when unset. Error: `refdoc: no scrape jobs`.
- `Dashboards(files map[string][]byte) (string, error)`: per file in name order, an H3 heading with the file name in a code span, "Title `<title>`, uid `<uid>`.", a table Variable, Multi, Query, and a table Panel, Type, Expression with one row per query target, nested row panels flattened as `deploy/kubernetes/base/grafana/dashboards_test.go` does, a panel without targets one row reading none. An expression holding `{{` or `}}` is `refdoc: %s: panel %q holds a mustache, render it fenced`. Errors: the `encoding/json` error with the file name, `refdoc: no dashboards`.

Every cell escapes `|` as `\|` and joins comment lines with one space. Every identifier, path, template, file name and literal a renderer emits is in a code span or a fenced block, so no brace reaches Vue's interpolation or the attribute syntax bare, and no renderer emits a heading above H3 or one whose first word starts lower-case outside a code span. A page places a block under a heading one level above the block's own headings: `Commands`, `AlertRules`, `Dashboards`, `OpenAPIOperations` and `OpenAPISchemas` emit H3 and sit under an H2; `Struct` and `JSONSchema` emit H4 and sit under an H3; the table-only renderers emit none.

### 5. Rules every page follows

Present tense, the built system; no rationale, a link to the explanation page that argues it instead. A placeholder in angle brackets is written in a code span. No heading skips a level and no hand-written heading is title case. A value copied by hand from a source with no renderer names that source in the sentence before it.

## Motivation

An integrator who wants the contract of an endpoint reads a 2608-line YAML file on GitHub; an operator who wants a default opens one of five `.env.example` files or the source; the export format is specified by example in a roadmap document written for a code generator; the alert expressions are read out of a manifest. Each is the first question of the first day, and the site answers it with an index that says the sidebar will list one page per surface "as each is published".

The explanation pages of #106 name the reference quadrant in plain text at five places because nothing was there to link, #108 cannot remove a monograph while its contract sections have no home, and #109 and #110 close each lesson by linking the page that specifies what the reader just used.

This change writes the 23 pages and renders 21 of them partly from the code, so a changed flag, setting, metric, rule or schema fails `go test ./...` until `make generate` refreshes the page: a page that cannot drift from the code without the build saying so.

## User Stories

- As an integrator calling the Reporting API, I want every endpoint with its parameters, bodies, responses and error types on one searchable page, so that I do not read the OpenAPI document by hand.
  - The endpoints page lists the 25 operations with the credential each needs, and the local search returns it for `ingestEvents`.
- As an operator deploying a service, I want every environment variable with its type, default, file-backed variant and meaning on one page, so that I configure the process without opening its source.
  - Each settings page lists every variable of the program's `EnvNames`; one added without a doc comment fails `go test ./docs/`.

items.title: P0 LMS/Factory: contrato SCORM único e certificação ponta a ponta dos 40 cursos
items.body:
## P0 — incidente sistêmico de confiabilidade dos 40 cursos EAD
Solicitação operacional: antes de disponibilizar até 40 cursos a aproximadamente 150 pessoas (até 6.000 realizações), reduzir risco de falha de progressão, retomada, avaliação e fechamento com um **contrato único para fábrica SCORM + player AirTrust**, sem patches específicos por curso.

### Evidências / lacuna suficiente
- O quality gate `lms-scorm-browser-run.ts` verifica launch / LMSInitialize / LMSCommit / unload / LMSFinish; **não completa nem reabre avaliações**. `applyRuntimeConformance()` pode declarar `publishable=true` mesmo com `completionReached=false` (teste canônico atualmente espera isso). Portanto `publishable` não é certificação pedagógica ponta a ponta.
- PBN: renovação EAD pendente de validação de elegibilidade e integração do fix #1322.
- MGO: 76% / 35 de 46 registrado, mas novo pacote abre em 1/46 após substituição: #1323.
- CFIT: versão estruturalmente incompatível, PR #1321 integrada; preservar bloqueio de transferência de conclusão.
- Doutrinamento Básico #15: #1311; ZIP candidato SHA256 `381ef573c6d88c1effe4d35c095ec676d245b0cf67336794e3f332457a0e340d` local QA PASS, ainda sem homologação/publicação.
- LGPD #69 e Regulação ANAC #23: issue já existente de pacotes publicados sem certificação possível.
- Auditoria geral read-only de cursos ativos disparada em [run #37986805929](https://github.com/Airtrust-Org/airtrust/actions/runs/37986805929) contra a produção SHA `9a7b137895c9f72a73808b78b258ed16dfe6a4bd`, Chromium + WebKit.

### Decisões arquiteturais
1. **Factory única e determinística** para novos conteúdos: HTML/CSS/JS de engine versionada e congelada, fonte de conteúdo declarativa, SCORM 1.2 Single SCO, raiz `imsmanifest.xml`, completion manifest V1, diagnostics V1. Proibir implementação da API SCORM ou de persistência de notas personalizada para cada curso.
2. **Padrão visual único**: grade consistente, responsiva, uso de imagens aeronáuticas reais e distintas, fonte principal >=20 px, navegação/quiz/feedback uniformes. Alterar o conteúdo não recompila comportamento específico.
3. **Contrato de estado**: `lesson_status`, `lesson_location`, `suspend_data` com IDs estáveis por slide e questão, revisão read-only após conclusão; estado isolado por matrícula/ciclo. Compatibilidade entre versões é declarada/testada; incompatibilidade não importa notas nem pula avaliações.
4. **Player único**: não criar `if (cursoId===...)` ou heurística de DOM para consertar SCORM artesanal; resume nativo apenas após comprovação de versão; validar cursor renderizado vs. marcador persistido; progresso exibido não prova retomada.
5. **Dois gates separados**: A) conformance técnica do protocolo; B) certificação funcional integral em navegador (first → suspend → resume → quiz insuficiente → quiz aprovado → finalize → reopen → no downgrade; duplo finish, revisão, versão compatível/incompatível, tenant/ciclo). Só chamar curso de **certificado** com ambos aprovados **para o SHA exato do ZIP e runtime candidato**.
6. **Inventário dos 40**: para cada curso, ID/tenant/hash/manifest/evidência/Chromium/WebKit/resultado por etapa/classificação (PASS, PACKAGE_FIX, PLAYER_FIX, UNCERTIFIED, NOT_APPLICABLE). Comparar versão publicada vs. candidata e não mascarar resultado com porcentagem.
7. **Bloqueio de liberação em massa** até existir evidência individual de todos os cursos designados, com piloto controlado e acompanhamento de telemetria de fechamento; preservar matrículas e históricos. Se teste falhar no harness/infra, classificar como inconclusivo, não falha comprovada de pacote nem PASS.
8. **Release**: usar GitHub/main, oito gates, staging, autorização SHA+artefato+escopo para produção. D1/R2 writes/matrículas reais somente com governança/autorização específica.

### Ordem / aceitação
- Reutilizar run read-only existente, tratar bloqueios em lote por causa técnica e sem retestes redundantes.
- Gerar contrato formal único Factory/AirTrust, tornar obrigatório no pipeline de geração de novos ZIPs e no intake LMS progressivamente (sem quebrar históricos legados).
- Corrigir lacuna do gate para diferenciar `protocol_pass` de `functional_certified`; nunca promover status funcional com apenas BrowserRun técnico.
- Certificar todos os pacotes ativos em staging/simulador isolado (Chromium e WebKit), registrar evidência e identificar candidatos que precisam de nova versão.
- Publicar apenas versões aprovadas pelo fluxo governado. Validar o caso real, e não somente unit tests.

**Não encerrar** só com issue, protocolo ou QA estático. Fechar depois de comprovar lote real e impedir recorrência para novos ZIPs.

items.body: Hi there, thanks for maintaining this repo! My company has been using it for a little while and it works really well. items.title: Release Train handoff — الحالة الحالية والمهام المتبقية — 2026-09-03
items.body:
# Release Train Handoff — 2026-09-03

هذا الـIssue هو نقطة الاستئناف الرسمية للمحادثات القادمة. الهدف: معرفة ما تم تنفيذه، ما بقي، وما هي بوابات النشر دون إعادة التشخيص من الصفر.

## الحالة العامة

- المستودع: `AMASI-SA/AMASI-SA`
- Production branch: `hotfix/prod-snap-meta-final`
- Git Production SHA المعروف: `1de6118484ac4fe1d0981e230618dbb573d8c58c`
- Live Production حاليًا ما زال على rollback القديم: `c320c293d1359060ae48931f091046a3e274b309`
- لا يوجد Merge/Publish/Republish معتمد للـRelease Train الحالي.
- Emergent gate يبقى مغلقًا حتى يصل تأكيد صريح أن `build-repair automation` تم تعطيله فعليًا لتطبيق `salla-analytics`.
- عند فتح gate لا ننشر المهام منفردة؛ الهدف النهائي: عدة PRs مستقلة → Final Production Source واحد → Release Intent v5 واحد جديد → Fresh Release Guard lease → **Republish واحد فقط** → verify.

---

# المهام المكتملة

## TASK 1 — Qoyod unsent-orders memory bounds

- PR: #1001
- الحالة: Draft / technically ready
- الهدف: منع heavy scans والضغط الذاكري في unsent-orders.
- تم: bounded cursors، single-flight، cache، concurrency ceiling، frontend polling/coalescing.
- لا تعيد تنفيذ نطاق #1001 في مهام أخرى.
- Release Intent الموجود داخل #1001 قديم خاص بهذه المهمة فقط، ولن يُستخدم كـFinal Intent إذا أضيفت بقية مهام Release Train.

## TASK 2 — Runtime Stability / Mongo / Auth

- PR: #1003
- Branch: `hotfix/runtime-stability-mongo-auth`
- Head: `d68e5fb20837ae935aa7755df436c26368e784a3`
- الحالة: Draft / technically ready
- تم:
  - Mongo pool/timeouts bounded.
  - Owner `/api/auth/me` fast-path يقلل DB reads.
  - transient DB failure → 503 وليس fake 401/logout.
  - Legacy Qoyod frozen polling خُفض من 5s إلى 300s.
  - Plan-B polling adaptive.
  - `/api/live` process-only و`/api/ready` Mongo bounded.
  - Auth retry coalescing.
- لا يوجد file overlap مع #1001.

## TASK 3 — Snapchat Spend Reliability

- PR: #1004
- Branch: `codex/snapchat-spend-reliability`
- Head: `a9d31c94db80b57cb558133c39effa64da92f94c`
- الحالة: Draft / technically ready
- تم:
  - per-day coverage diagnostics.
  - 29/30 يبقى fail-closed لكن يكشف اليوم الناقص بدل `لا بيانات` فقط.
  - targeted retry لليوم المفقود فقط.
  - parent/child run proof alignment.
  - V2 financial scheduler writer authority كل 10 دقائق، selected accounts فقط، lease/single-flight.
  - فصل `last_mezan_check_at` عن provider success/value-change/fact timestamps.
  - منع تحويل incomplete Snapchat إلى final `0.00` أو صافي ربح مزيف.
- لا يوجد file overlap مع #1001/#1003.

## TASK 4 — Salla Missing Orders Reliability

- PR: #1005
- Branch: `codex/salla-missing-orders-reliability`
- Head: `c2c19032b052d7eb3af1d78c86ac3d7ab2ed46e3`
- الحالة: Draft / technically ready
- الملفات: فقط
  - `backend/salla_integration/auto_sync.py`
  - `backend/salla_integration/routes.py`
  - `backend/tests/test_salla_order_discovery_reliability.py`
- root causes reproduced:
  1. checkpoint كان يتقدم رغم فشل طلب فردي، فيمكن أن يخرج الطلب من overlap ويضيع.
  2. discovery كان `page=1`, `per_page=60` فقط، فيفقد الطلب 61+.
- تم:
  - bounded pagination.
  - durable tenant-scoped checkpoint + retry ledger.
  - 24–48h read-first gap reconciliation.
  - missing-only recovery؛ existing webhook orders لا تُكتب من جديد.
  - no background `GET /orders/{id}`.
  - fixture: Salla 192 / Mezan 190 → recover exactly 2 → 192/192 دون rewrite للـ190.
- لا يوجد file overlap مع #1001/#1003/#1004.

## TASK 5A — Preparation Duplicate Units Root Cause Diagnosis

- الحالة: **Diagnosis only — مكتمل تشخيص الكود، لا PR**.
- الطلبات الموثقة:
  - `279346733` — PF `PF-20260829-0092`
  - `279383684` — PF `PF-20260829-0085`
- المؤكد على مستوى الكود:
  - `order_items_with_review_snapshot()` يدمج فقط عند exact `order_item_id`، ومصالحة الهوية التجارية تعمل فقط عندما Snapshot ID فارغ.
  - إذا Current line وReview Snapshot يمثلان نفس القطعة لكن لديهما `order_item_id` مختلف وغير فارغ، يمكن أن يدخل Snapshot كسطر جديد.
  - بعدها يصبح لكل تمثيل Ready IDs / allocations / Batch lines / PDF cards مستقلة.
- التصنيف المثبت: التكرار ليس PDF-only؛ وصل إلى physical preparation workflow قبل PDF.
- `buy_as_gift` ليس له branch سببي مثبت في identity/allocation path.
- sender/receiver phone ليس جزءًا من item identity path.
- **مهم:** incident-specific historical cause للطلبين لم يُثبت 100% بعد لأن Stages 3–11 لم تُقرأ بكل IDs الفعلية؛ لذلك لا تدّعِ أن Salla بريئة تاريخيًا أو أن H2/H3 ثبتت للحالتين بعينهما دون قراءة projections.
- المرشحون تاريخيًا: 45 PDF منطقيًا، 19 ملفًا فيها repeated order numbers، 21 order candidates، 40 excess-card candidates؛ هذه ليست Bugs مؤكدة حتى تُقارن بالـauthoritative quantity/options/source identity.

---

# المهمة التالية — TASK 5B

## Preparation Unit Identity Reconciliation

**ابدأ بهذه المهمة قبل TASK 6.**

### المرحلة 5B.0 — Evidence completion read-only

للطلبين `279346733` و`279383684` حاول قراءة فقط:
- `unified_orders.products`
- `raw_by_source.salla_direct.items` إن كانت محفوظة
- `workflow.items`
- review snapshot identity
- allocations
- batch stored lines

واربط المعرفين:
- `02937e4c63aa5fa3a3452bcaf97d610c`
- `87097cf3b19d5be3aec25e5495f02e15`

إذا ثبت Current ID != Snapshot ID مع نفس authoritative commercial identity وquantity=1 → `incident_root_cause_confirmed=true`.
إذا لم تتوفر projections الكافية → لا تخمّن؛ استخدم `code_defect_confirmed=true` و`incident_root_cause_confirmed=false` ثم نفذ الإصلاح الوقائي فقط.

### Root fix المطلوب

- exact `order_item_id` أولًا.
- ثم stable `source_item_id` عندما يكون موثوقًا.
- fallback commercial identity فقط في One-to-One unambiguous case:
  `order_number + product/parent/variant/SKU + canonical options/customization fingerprint`.
- لا dedupe أعمى.
- ambiguity → Fail Closed / keep distinct.
- حافظ على quantity=2 الحقيقية، السطور Provider الحقيقية المتطابقة، ونفس SKU بخيارات/تخصيص مختلف.

### Authoritative quantity guard

الحارس يجب أن يكون لكل:

`user_id + order_number + authoritative_commercial_line_key`

**ولا تجعل `unit_index` جزءًا من مفتاح التجميع.**

Invariant:

`committed_active_units + planned_units <= authoritative_quantity`

ثم تحقق منفصلًا أن unit indices unique وداخل `1..authoritative_quantity`.

نفذ الحارس قبل allocation commit ثم قبل Batch/PDF finalization.

### Ready IDs

لا تغير `stable_ready_item_id()` أو `stable_ready_unit_id()` أو format/algorithm للهويات إلا إذا أثبت اختبار failing أن الإصلاح مستحيل بدون ذلك؛ لأن تغييرها قد يجعل historical allocations صحيحة تبدو stale/orphaned.

### Expected initial scope

ابدأ بالحد الأدنى:
- `backend/reviewed_products_catalog.py`
- `backend/reviewed_preparation_batches.py`
- tests

أضف `reviewed_preparation_v3.py` أو mobile routes فقط عند ضرورة مثبتة.

- Draft PR مستقل.
- لا Release Intent أثناء التنفيذ الأولي.
- لا data cleanup/backfill للطلبات القديمة.
- لا تعديل أو حذف PF التاريخية.

---

# TASK 6 — Products V2 / Salla Publish Reliability

ابدأها **بعد TASK 5B** في Draft PR مستقل.

الصفحة المتأثرة مثالًا:

`/products-v2?missing_mezan_cost=1&sold_only=1&from=2026-09-03&to=2026-09-03&product=mpv2_358058139&focus=cost`

الأعراض المثبتة من UI والكود:

1. Cloudflare origin error: `The origin web server sent a response that Cloudflare could not parse...`.
2. الصفحة قد تعرض تفاصيل منتج محدد بينما القائمة تقول `0 منتج` / لا توجد منتجات ناقصة تكلفة.
3. `product=` يختار المنتج المفتوح، بينما filtered cohort يستخدم مسارًا مختلفًا و`product_ids` عند الحاجة؛ direct cost link قد يعمل full cohort scan بلا داعٍ.
4. فتح المنتج ينفذ `refreshProductV2Details()` مع cost read في `Promise.all`؛ refresh يقرأ Salla live `GET /products/{id}` ثم يكتب Mongo/detail log وقد يحدث cost revision.
5. بالتالي محرر تكلفة ميزان المحلي يعتمد على Salla availability؛ هذا يجب فصله.
6. list path قد ينتظر `syncRecentProductsV2()` قبل العرض.
7. `MezanProductsAutoSync` ينفذ force recent sync كل 60s عندما الصفحة مفتوحة.
8. publish الحالي إلى Salla متزامن طويل: GET current → PUT update → GET verify → وقد يوجد PUT rollback عند verification mismatch.
9. إذا PUT نجح ثم verification timeout، generic failure لا يعني أن التعديل لم يصل؛ نحتاج `publish_outcome=unknown` / reconciliation بدل blind re-PUT.

### Target architecture

- **Local-first product editor:** عرض بيانات Mezan + Cost Profile فورًا، بلا Salla blocking وبلا Mongo write لمجرد فتح الصفحة.
- direct product cost path عند `product=...&focus=cost` بدل full sold cohort scan.
- فصل selected product عن filtered cohort حتى لا يظهر 0 products مع تفاصيل وكأنها ضمن القائمة.
- local Mezan cost save لا يعتمد على Salla.
- Salla refresh يكون background غير مانع أو زر صريح.
- publish state machine واضحة: `preparing → publishing → verifying → succeeded` أو `verification_pending/outcome_unknown/failed/rollback_required`.
- لا blind retry بعد unknown outcome.
- API transient errors يجب أن ترجع JSON منظمًا بدل origin response ناقص/غير قابل للتفسير.
- راجع force-sync كل 60s؛ اجعله non-blocking, single-flight, no overlap with publish، أو أبطأ/event-driven حسب القياس.
- UI يظهر مرحلة النشر الحالية والخطأ المحدد.
- Mezan internal cost fields تبقى protected؛ `salla_cost_price` فقط الحقل التجاري المسموح صراحة للنشر عند الحاجة.

---

# ترتيب Freeze / Release النهائي

لا تنفذ هذه المرحلة حتى:

items.title: Generic File Tap/Target
items.body:
Migrated from GitLab: https://gitlab.com/meltano/sdk/-/issues/242

Originally created by @vischous on 2021-10-18 15:21:44

---

A generic file based tap seems appropriate, going to call this `tap-file` for now to give a name to it, pardon the words I chose here I'd be happy to update the Ontology used :D 

Today there's a bunch of ideasthat overlap with the core idea of File. I haven't seen a "connector" tool handle this very well before this is a common issue (Fivetran, workato, etc etc). 

Where we are today:
- https://hub.meltano.com/taps/s3-csv
- https://hub.meltano.com/taps/csv
- https://hub.meltano.com/taps/gmail-csv (questionable if this should be on the list)
- https://hub.meltano.com/taps/parquet
- https://hub.meltano.com/taps/sftp
- https://hub.meltano.com/targets/jsonl
- https://hub.meltano.com/targets/csv
- https://hub.meltano.com/targets/azureblobstorage

To make this generic, we'd need some standard features. 

File Tap/Target needed **Features**
1. Transport Layer (I think the right term, maybe something else) - How do we get the file, FTP, SFTP, S3, POST(curl), etc etc etc
1. File Types - CSV, Parquet, JSONL, etc etc
1. Compression - gzip, zip, 7zip, tar, [gzip ](https://meltano.slack.com/archives/C01PKLU5D1R/p1634570689373600), etc
1. Encoding's should be handled in some way that makes sense

Other Ideas that could be guiding principles for the design of this
1. Identity Functionality should work. ie `meltano elt tap-file target-file` should output the same file with no changes (cksum `filein` == chksum `fileout` ) 
2. https://github.com/edgarrmondragon/tap-dbf/pull/1/files from @edgarrmondragon  uses [pyfilesystem2](https://www.pyfilesystem.org/page/index-of-filesystems/) which seems like a nice abstraction layer for all of this. 
    1. URI's for everything  `uri: datalake://{username}:{password}@{storage_name}?tenant_id={tenant_id}`
3. Example configuration with sensible defaults
    1. Default to pulling all files from the base directory 

Questions
1. Does a single `tap-file` make the most sense?
1. Does a library with helpful functionality make sense instead, and just have everyone implement 


This comes up in different ways, and I'd like to collect ideas in one place (I keep posting the same information and maybe it's just a bad idea so let's have one place to hash out the idea :D ) 
1. https://meltano.slack.com/archives/C013EKWA2Q1/p1619166461259200
1. https://meltano.slack.com/archives/C01PKLU5D1R/p1634567772367800
1. https://meltano.slack.com/archives/C01V8L0NZC1/p1626475132026300
1. https://github.com/hotgluexyz/target-csv/issues/6
1. https://github.com/MeltanoLabs/target-athena/issues/27
